ld_json.name: The Inn at Little Washington
ld_json.description:
Patrick O’Connell’s inspired American cuisine draws admirers from around the world. Dining at The Inn at Little Washington has been likened to performance art with the guest always playing the starring role. The experience evokes a romantic dinner party in a private country house from another era. Whimsical touches such as a rolling cow (named Faira) displaying cheeses invite guests to relax, be themselves, and have fun.

Patrick’s approach to cooking, while paying homage to the lawmakers of Classical French Cuisine, reflects a belief in American cuisine today-- healthy, eclectic, imaginative, unrestricted by ethnic boundaries and always growing. Much of the produce and herbs used in the restaurant is raised on a small farm on our campus by our Farmer in Residence, Andy Thewlis. Throughout the last four decades, The Inn has established a network of local farmers and suppliers whose products represent the best in our region. In 2021, Michelin awarded The Inn a Green Star for sustainability.

content.body: After taking the Parisian dining scene by storm, acclaimed chef Daniel Rose brings home the James Beard "Best New Restaurant" award for his very first stateside restaurant. Located in SoHo, the space is a gracious modern nod to fine European gastronomy, with crisp linens, flickering candles, and whitewashed brick. Updating classical French cuisine with charm and verve, Rose shrinks the intercontinental divide separating the City of Light and the Big Apple, proving that the true essence of fine French dining can thrive in any time zone.

ld_json.name: Auberge du Soleil
ld_json.description:
For many, the name Auberge du Soleil is synonymous with wine country cuisine. Founded in 1981 by visionary French restaurateur Claude Rouas as Napa Valley’s first fine-dining establishment, The Restaurant has maintained its legacy as a “must experience” culinary destination for more than 40 years. 

Join us for a casual à la carte dining experience in The Bar or indulge in a Michelin guided multi course experience in The Restaurant. Executive Chef Robert Curry sources the freshest ingredients from local purveyors, harvested at their peak of flavor, to create delicious dishes showcasing the region's best seasonal ingredients.

Celebrating 18 consecutive Michelin Star awards, The Restaurant at Auberge du Soleil provides a memorable feast for the eyes and the senses. Nestled within a sun-lit hillside overlooking lush vineyards and distant mountains, the spectacular vista views from the intimate dining room or the expansive outdoor terrace serve as an idyllic backdrop for one of wine country's most renown fine dining experiences. Showcasing fresh, seasonal ingredients, sourced from local purveyors, the Mediterranean-inspired menu is complemented by an extensive selection of international wines from The Restaurant’s award-winning 15,000 bottle cellar.

ld_json.description: Michelin-recommended and locally loved, Homer St. Cafe and Bar is a vibrant, casual dining destination perfect for lunch with friends, lively happy hours, birthday celebrations, and group gatherings.Located in the historic Homer building in Vancouver’s Yaletown district, our charming space blends vintage character with modern energy. Whether you're pulling up a seat at the Chef’s Bar to watch our culinary team in action, enjoying a cozy booth under antique tiles, or hosting a group in our semi-private dining room, the atmosphere is always warm, welcoming, and fun.Our rotisserie turns out juicy, responsibly raised chicken, ribs, and steaks daily—perfectly portioned for solo diners or shared feasts. With plenty of gluten-free options, crave-worthy sides, and a bold cocktail and wine list, we’ve got something for everyone.Join us for lunch, swing by for happy hour, or plan your next birthday celebration—Homer St. Cafe and Bar is where comfort food and good times come together.

review.reviewBody: Great place to grab brunch. Historic old building, nice patio to dine in the am with reflective sun off buildings. Great service and tasty innovative dishes. Gets pretty crowded so recommended to book a table
Fantastic service and food. I would describe the noise level as loud, it was difficult to converse where we were seated. I would definitely go back if a calmer area is available in this restaurant.

The ambience is beautiful overlooking the boats in the bay. The service was very good unfortunately we ordered the fish and chips and the batter was very soggy underneath, but the fish itself was cooked very well.
Best house red in town, and their burger was 👌🏻. I asked for a quiet spot and they seated us in an upper room - so appreciated. Excellent service too. Love this place!
Great location, atmosphere and overall dining experience.

We made a reservation for breakfast, and before we were even seated, our server let us know there was another reservation after us, so we would need to be finished within an hour. That made the whole experience feel very rushed. I understand that restaurants get busy, but one hour is simply not enough time to order, enjoy coffee or drinks, wait for the food, and eat at a normal pace.
The food was excellent, and the service was okay, but the atmosphere was very uncomfortable because it was freezing inside. I was shivering the entire time, and the couple beside us also mentioned how cold it was. I couldn’t even take my jacket off while eating, which made the experience far less enjoyable overall.
Wonderful dinner!  Kahn was a a new server but was very attentive, friendly and a fantastic server!   Thank you!
We shared four small plates that were absolutely fantastic. Great service from Dani! ￼
Awesome service, incredible food, great experience. I am a repeat customer and Homer St. Cafe never fails.
Excellent food, service and ambiance. Terrific spot for food and drinks!

about.body: Safta means ‘grandmother’ in Hebrew, and though our grandma’s place never looked as sleek as Alon Shaya’s beautiful Denver debut, there’s something instantly warm and soothing about it. The James Beard Award-winning chef cooks up an Israeli-focused menu, with influences from Yemen, Syria, Morocco and Greece thrown in.

need_to_know.body:
Parties of all sizes from 1-14 people can book online! All parties of 8 or more guests automatically select our Chef Entrust menu, a prix fixe, family-style offering of all of our favorites priced at $70/per person. Beverage, tax, and gratuity are charged separately.  Please be sure to note any allergies or dietary restrictions when booking your reservation.

Please note that we are unable to combine reservations booked separately.  When making a reservation, be sure to include children (including toddlers and infants in strollers/carriers) in the total guest count.

Element 47, a Michelin Guide-recommended restaurant, is Aspen’s finest spot to wine, dine and unwind. The name Element 47 pays tribute to silver, the precious metal that first put Aspen on the map. Whether you ski in for lunch, drop in at the bar for a more casual rendezvous, a celebration, or just to experience our Colorado Contemporary dinner cuisine, you’ll be greeted with warmth, not formality.

ld_json.name: Mercantile
ld_json.description:
Every plate at Mercantile tells a story—of the land, the season, and the hands that brought it to life. Helmed by Executive Chef Alex Grenier and guided by Founding Chef Alex Seidel's vision, Mercantile celebrates Colorado’s best purveyors, crafting hyper-seasonal dishes that are elegant in their simplicity and prepared with intention.

Lunch offers two paths: a relaxed counter-service café with fresh, vibrant fare or a thoughtfully curated two-course experience in the dining room.

Dinner is an invitation to connect. Guests gather around the table, choosing from dishes inspired by Earth, Sea, Grain, and Pasture—or they can hand over the reins and let us craft an unforgettable meal. Courses arrive in waves, designed to be savored and shared.

It’s more than a meal—it’s a collection of moments, meant to be remembered.

Awaken your senses during breakfast to the delicate aromas of freshly baked pastries, and embark on a tantalising journey inspired by the sun-kissed landscapes of the French and Italian rivieras. Enjoy a rendezvous with the finest flavours at Riviera by Jean Imbert. Our elegant set lunch is designed to delight – and served speedily, so you can make the most of your afternoon. Enjoy weekday lunches like never before. Embark on a gastronomic journey through sun-kissed landscapes for dinner, complemented by exclusive wines and breathtaking views of the shimmering Marasi Bay Marina and iconic Burj Khalifa. Jean Imbert, voted Chef of the Year 2019 by GQ and one of the 50 Most Influential French People by Vanity Fair, Jean Imbert’s accolades make quite the introduction.

ld_json.name: Jara by Martín Berasategui
ld_json.description: At Jara, there’s magic in the air. Here the flavour-drenched alchemy of fire dances with delight. Experience a mesmerising of the senses, for this is the story of authenticity: of true Basque cooking in the hands of a master craftsman who relishes in serving up his passion. As the first chef to open a Basque restaurant in Dubai, 12 Michelin-starred chef Martín Berasategui is set to shake up Dubai’s dining scene. Expect exceptional cooking accompanied by a warm, welcoming energy that lights up the room each night. This atmospheric restaurant acts as a creative ode to our celebrated chef's native Basque Country. Here Martín Berasategui brings together the spirit of life, passion, warmth, and family - all dancing in the fire of the kitchen. Come for the food and the sense of theatre, but be prepared to be captivated by sweeping city views. This is an elevated dining experience in more ways than one.

ld_json.name: Sushi Sho - NYC
ld_json.description:
Chef Keiji Nakazawa began his culinary journey at the age of 15, undergoing training at 20 different Japanese and sushi restaurants across Japan. In 1989, he opened "すし匠" Sushi Sho in Yotsuya, Tokyo, and currently oversees operations at thirty establishments, including independent restaurants operated by chefs who trained under Chef Nakazawa. In 2016, he made his international debut, opening Sushi Sho at The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Waikiki Beach. In 2023, he opened Terakoya (private school) Sushi Sho in Azabudai Hills. In 2024, he opened Sushi Sho in New York City.

Sho's Experience at Hinoki Sushi Counter
Initially, we will be offering a Shorter Omakase, a curated culinary journey designed to showcase the finest ingredients and craftsmanship by our chefs. For those seeking to enhance their dining adventure, we will also provide Okonomi options as supplements. Chef Nakazawa aims to promote the essence of traditional "Okonomi" at Sushi Sho in New York, providing diners with the freedom to choose what they want to eat.

Omakase
The term “Omakase” means “I’ll leave it up to you” in Japanese, indicating that diners trust chef’s expertise to choose and present a variety of dishes.
Omakase style made famous by Chef Nakazawa with his close sushi chefs around 1989 in Japan. 
Sushi Sho has been offering “Shorter Omakase” tasting menu and “Okonomi” that customers choose whatever they want from today’s selection as supplements. That way our customers enjoy chef’s choice and their own favorite topping same time.

Okonomi
The term "Okonomi" translates to "what you like" or "what you want" in Japanese. Diners have the flexibility to customize their sushi by selecting various ingredients, offering a more personalized dining experience compared to omakase. 
Note: Okonomi was the main ordering method at traditional sushi restaurants approximately 30 years ago.

Edomae 
Edomae-zushi puts the spotlight on the shari (sushi rice). It involves meticulous treatment of the fish to complement the shari. Various treatments such as vinegar marination and kelp pressing, along with thorough temperature management of the ingredients and shari, creates a harmonious unity between the shari and the ingredients. "Sushi Sho's" Edomae-zushi maximizes the inherent flavors of the ingredients.

Tip-free establishment
Both cash and credit card gratuities will be respectfully declined. 
Reflecting the Japanese custom, exceptional hospitality is an integral part of the Sushi Sho dining experience and is provided to every guest.

Photography and videography policy
Our photography policy aligns with our commitment to creating memorable moments for each guest.
Embracing the Moment: We encourage our guests to fully immerse themselves in the sushi journey and ambiance we've crafted. In an effort to enhance your experience and ensure everyone's enjoyment, we kindly request that you refrain from taking pictures or recording videos during your visit to Sushi Sho.

Reasoning:
            1.	Savor the Experience: Our wish is for you to savor every moment without distractions, allowing you to fully appreciate the flavors, artistry, and ambiance that define Sushi Sho.
            2.	Respecting Privacy: Some diners prefer not to be photographed, and by refraining from these activities, we contribute to a more private and comfortable dining environment.

Your understanding and cooperation in adhering to this policy are greatly appreciated. Our aim is to provide an atmosphere where each guest can relish the present, creating memories that go beyond visuals.

Neighbors
Book an NYC getaway at our neighboring hotel, Andaz 5th Avenue. Experience luxury accommodations in the heart of midtown.
URL: https://www.hyatt.com/andaz/nycam-andaz-5th-avenue

Sushi Sho maintains a refined atmosphere and, therefore, does not admit guests under the age of 13.

content.name: why_we_like_it
content.title: Why We Like It

about.body: Le Bernardin, New York's internationally acclaimed four-star seafood restaurant, opened in 1986. Owned by Maguy Le Coze and Chef Eric Ripert, the celebrated restaurant earned a four-star review from The New York Times just three months after opening and has maintained this four-star status for the past thirty years. Le Bernardin currently ranks No. 44 on the World’s 50 Best Restaurants list and has held three stars from the Michelin Guide since the guide’s 2005 New York launch. The New York Zagat Guide consistently recognizes Le Bernardin as top ranking in the categories of Food, Service, and Popularity. Most recently, Le Bernardin was ranked first in America and first in the world by La Liste, the global food guide and review aggregator. With a focus on the freshest ingredients prepared simply, at Le Bernardin their mantra says it all: The Fish is the Star of the Plate.

need_to_know.body:
We are excited to welcome you to Le Bernardin! 
•	Our DRESS CODE is “business casual”.  Jackets are recommended for gentleman, but not required. Shorts, t-shirts, short sleeves, flip-flops, sweatshirts, sweatpants and sneakers are not permitted.  
•	We accept major credit cards and cash payments.
•	Reservations are required for the main Dining Room; our Lounge is walk-in based
•	Credit card is required to make a reservation and cancellation policy is 48 hours prior to your 
        reservation date to avoid $150 per person fee. 
•	Lunch is served Monday to Friday. Dinner is served Monday to Saturday.  We are closed on 
        Sunday.   
•	We welcome young guests 10 years and older who would like to experience our menu.  We 
        offer prix fixe menu and tasting menus. No a la carte menu options in the main dining room.
•	We reconfirm every reservation. Reservations made without valid contact information will be canceled. 

We look forward to welcoming you!

ld_json.name: Jungsik
ld_json.description:
Jungsik offers a modern and unique understanding of contemporary Korean cuisine – innovative chef Yim has christened it as New Korean. The name for the restaurant, Jungsik, was a play on words. In the Korean language Jung Sik is a formal dinner and it is also the name of our chef. We invite you to come and experience the boldly flavored and whimsical culinary offerings of restaurant Jungsik.

We are able to accommodate most allergies and dietary restrictions if we are notified properly in advance. We will not be able to accommodate guests with allergies to either soy or garlic.

Children over the age of 12 are welcome in the dining room.

content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Eleven Madison Park is an award-winning fine dining restaurant located in the heart of New York City. The restaurant overlooks Madison Square Park, one of the most beautiful parks in Manhattan, and sits at the base of a historic Art Deco building on the corner of East 24th Street and Madison Avenue. Eleven Madison Park has evolved significantly under Chef Daniel Humm's leadership in food and experience, earning several accolades, including 4 stars from the New York Times and 3 stars from the Michelin guide.

need_to_know.body:
We offer a Full Tasting menu served in our main dining room, and a four-to-five course Bar Tasting menu served at tables in our lounge. Please note, since mid-October 2025, guests will have the option to enjoy a fully plant-based menu, or to include select animal proteins in a few courses of their meal. 

Reservations for the month of May will become available exclusively online on Monday, April 1st at 10:00am.

All reservations are booked exclusively online through Resy. To confirm reservations, we take payment in full for the tasting menus and those sales are final and non-refundable. We do not offer cancellation or rescheduling options. For any questions on policies please contact infoEMP@elevenmadisonpark.com.

We can accommodate parties of up to 7 guests in the main dining room and 4 in the lounge. We have availability for parties of 8 or more in our Private Dining Room on our second floor. For parties of 8 or more, please inquire about our private dining and restaurant buyout options on our website.

For the comfort and enjoyment of all of our guests, we kindly ask that no excessive flash photography or ​disruptive photographic equipment be used in our dining room or bar area. For more details, please visit the FAQ portion of our website: elevenmadisonpark.com.

why_we_like_it.body: Because EMP's kitchen team continues to push the boundaries of what food should look and taste like in surprising, creative, and thoughtful ways, making a meal here something truly special and unforgettable.

review.reviewBody: Maybe my expectations were too high… it was a good experience and the staff are awesome… but the food was just… fine. There really wasn’t anything that stood out as ‘if I have 24 hours to live I want to go back and have XXX…’, like the Foie Gras Nigiri at Uchi in Austin.
They were so sweet and gave me a set of coasters for my new house but they were lost in the uber last night 😭

Had a wonderful once in a lifetime meal could not be happier! The staff, the food, the steps of service everything felt very intentional and nothing was gratuitous. The experience was interactive, genuine and delicious . Thank you to everyone!

My only complaint is that we were seated near an automatic draft of air which meant we were extremely cold every 20 min or so and there was nothing we could do about it.

Molecular cuisine at its best, amazing chemistry & biochemistry.... beautiful presentations...A few negative things:  a little bit too long wait at the bar mini before dinner.... maybe another drink or bite would have been nice... to make the wait a little less unpleasant...On the service...kind of robotic service....they looked tired and ... not engaged...although we were the first dinner of the of the first day of the week... A major issue... they were stingy with wine.. this was really almost unpleasant... at this price, you can be a bit more generous, virtually no refills after pouring a few milliliters of wine.... maybe the guests should bring their own bottles and pay cork fee.. .so to have a real wine pairing...Overall it was nice experience but not exceptional... BTW, we went there to celebrate our two birthdays ... got some kind of  cheap cookies... no we did not miss the whole kitchen plus singing Happy Birthday out of tune.. but at this level a restaurant can do better...  the highlight was the dishes..... and see what the best molecular cuisine can prepare...asking if we would go back... probably not....

We so enjoyed our night at Minibar. It' was our 11th visit and they still wow us as with delicious course after course. The food was flavorful and plated whimsically. The wine pairings were particularly great this year and I would 100% recommend it if you are a wine lover.

This was a truly exceptional experience. We dined here for the first time. We had the most enjoyable time. Each plate was unique, flavorful, and a work of art. Alex- our host- was exeptional- her wine pairings for the night outstanding. This was an experience of a lifetime.

￼

This was a wonderful dining experience and I honestly don’t know what more they need to do for a 3rd star.   The service was so amazing.   Down to earth team who seriously made the evening that much more enjoyable.  Highly recommend!
Excellent food, service and ambience.  Recommend highly.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, minibar by José Andrés is an excellent pick for date night or other special occasions. The restaurant offers an intimate, theatrical tasting-menu experience with impeccable service, creative presentations and a dedicated barmini for pre-dinner cocktails. It’s pricey and designed as a multi-course chef’s counter experience, so book in advance, dress business-casual, and consider adding the wine pairing or stopping at barmini beforehand for a full evening.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have accessible or family-friendly seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, staff are accommodating and have made special arrangements for guests with accessibility needs and families. Guests report sign language interpreters, description cards, and thoughtful allergy substitutions. Keep in mind the dining room is very intimate with counter seating, so while families and teens do dine here, it’s a formal tasting experience best suited to older children and those comfortable with a small, theatrical setting.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to minibar by José Andrés?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best time is for a planned special occasion or celebration on a weekday evening when the pace can feel a bit calmer, many guests recommend letting the team know it’s a celebration so they can personalize touches. If you prefer a relaxed flow, avoid the very first seating (some guests felt that sitting rushed) and consider combining the meal with pre-dinner cocktails at barmini.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The atmosphere is intimate, theatrical and highly curated, think playful, avant‑garde fine dining with close-up service. Guests praise the precision, presentation and joyful service, though some note the room can be lively: music, a loud private party, or occasional cooking odors/HVAC issues have been mentioned. Overall, it’s a warm yet dramatic setting best for diners who enjoy chef‑driven tasting experiences.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for minibar by José Andrés?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dress code is business casual. Guests typically dress up for the occasion, many visit for anniversaries and celebrations, so smart, neat attire is appropriate. If you’re celebrating, a slightly dressier outfit fits the refined, Michelin-starred environment.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant kid-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Families do dine here, and guests have brought teens and celebrated birthdays with children. That said, minibar is a formal, multi-course tasting experience with no kids’ menu and an intimate counter setting, so it’s best for older children who can sit through a lengthy tasting. If bringing younger kids, call ahead to discuss timing and accommodations.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to minibar by José Andrés?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you prefer a slightly calmer service, choose a weekday evening, Tuesday through Thursday, when the room is often less crowded than weekend seatings. Any night is special for celebrations, but weekdays can offer a steadier pace and a more relaxed experience. Book early regardless of day, as counter seating is limited.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any special awards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, minibar by José Andrés is a multi‑year Michelin-recognized restaurant, holding two Michelin stars (listed for 2023, 2024 and 2025). Guests and critics consistently praise its high-level technique, presentation and service that support these accolades.

about.body:
The award-winning, Michelin-Starred central NYC restaurant offers a comfortably luxurious, upscale Contemporary-French-American and Alsatian-inspired dining experience with a distinct New York spirit. Gabriel Kreuther looks out onto NYC's vibrant Bryant Park on 42nd street and offers casual, fine-dining.

Restaurant Gabriel Kreuther has been named one of The Best Restaurants in the USA by The Daily Meal, Wine Enthusiast, Opinionated About Dining, Gayot, and Business Insider and is also an exclusive member of Relais & Châteaux. Gabriel Kreuther Restaurant earned the prestigious AAA 5-Diamond Awards, The Best New Restaurant of the Year Award from NYC's Village Voice 2015, Three Stars from The New York Times and Two Michelin Stars. Gabriel Kreuther restaurant is the recipient of the Wine Spectator Grand Award.

need_to_know.body:
We are open for dinner Monday through Thursday from 4:45pm to 9:30pm and Friday-Saturday from 4:45pm to 10:00pm. In our Dining Room, Bar and Lounge, we offer a 3-course pre theatre menu at $155 (available from 4:45 to 5:30pm) a 3-course prix fixe menu at $200, a 4-course prix fixe menu at $235 and a 6-course tasting menu at $325. Guests are also welcome to enjoy our à la carte menu in the Bar and Lounge.

We are open for lunch on Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, from 12pm to 2pm, offering our à la carte and three-course prix fixe menus in the Dining Room.

ld_json.name: Masa
ld_json.description:
Chef Masayoshi Takayama apprenticed under the direction of sushi master, Suhiyama Toshiaki, at Tokyo’s famed Ginza Sushi-ko where he learned to appreciate an intimate relationship with food and dining to create a full sensory experience. After moving up the ranks under the tutelage of his revered master, Chef Masa followed a boyhood ambition to travel to the U.S. to open his own restaurant — and play lots of golf. In Los Angeles, he opened Ginza Sushi Ko in 1987, an homage to his former teacher, where he taught himself to combine classic and modern techniques to serve dishes inspired by tradition, yet inflected with his creative spirit. A move to New York on the advice of friend Chef Thomas Keller came ten years later, and Masa opened its doors in 2004. 

A solid hinoki wood sushi counter is the focal point of the otherwise simple décor at Masa, allowing the ingredients and dishes to shine. The courses build on seasonal properties utilized only in their freshest, most quintessential state. Each course is served on plateware designed by Chef Masa himself, through his ceramics vertical Masa Designs, chosen to complement the dish's ideal visual and gastronomic appeal.

content.body:
Joo Ok is a Korean fine dining restaurant founded in 2016 by Chef Chang ho Shin. Originally recognized as a two-starred restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul, Joo Ok has brought its philosophy and cuisine to New York, where it currently holds two MICHELIN star from 2025.

The name Joo Ok, which can be interpreted as “threading precious jade marbles,” symbolizes not only elegance and precision, but also Chef Shin’s desire to welcome guests into a space that feels like his own home — warm, thoughtful, and deeply personal. At Joo Ok, the freshest seasonal ingredients meet time-honored Korean seasonings and ‘jang’ (Korean mother sauces) to create a dining experience rooted in tradition and refined with a contemporary touch.

We invite you to the Hanok-setting experience with an 12-course tasting menu curated by Chef Shin.

ld_json.description:
Odo is open for lunch and dinner service from Tuesday through Sunday.

The Lounge is open from Tuesday through Sunday.

Please note that reservations at the lounge do not offer our Kaiseki Tasting Experience.

Cancellations can be refunded up to 48 hours from the reservation.  Any cancellations made within 48 hours, as well as no shows will not be refunded.

about.body: Join Chef Max Natmessnig and Marco Prins as they take you on a culinary journey using Japanese and French techniques. Our 14 course tasting menu will be a life long memory which will be cherished.

need_to_know.body:
Our tasting menu primarily consists of seafood.  We are unable to accommodate vegan, vegetarian, celiac and kosher diets, soy, mushroom, lemon & lime allergies, and No Seafood requests. Kindly notify us of any allergies or dietary restrictions at least 48 hours in advance of your reservation. Our menu is crafted to be enjoyed in its entirety to fully enhance the flavor experience. We cannot accommodate any allergies or dietary restrictions upon arrival. 

While we take every precaution in the handling and preparation of food, complete avoidance of cross-contamination cannot be guaranteed. Our kitchen uses shared equipment and preparation areas, and therefore guests with severe allergies should be aware that trace contact may still occur despite our best efforts.

We charge $385 a person before tax and gratuity. A $200 deposit is required upon reservation.

Prompt arrival is crucial to ensure an optimal dining experience, so please make sure all members of your party arrive punctually.  Late arrivals of 15 minutes or more may or may not be accommodated, and may result in missed courses. 

Our staff reserves the right to refuse service to guests who do not comply with our policy. Additionally, we kindly request that all guests adhere to the dress code is business casual attire with Suit jackets are recommended for all gentlemen in the dining room. But not required. We do not allow shorts, T- Shirts, sweatpants, hats, or flip-flops. While we welcome pictures and videos, we ask that you are respectful of the other guests dining with you. 

Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare is available for private dinners, with the option to reserve the entire space for an exclusive evening. Please note that a minimum of two months' notice is required to secure your date from public reservations.

ld_json.name: Atomix
ld_json.description: Ato, stemming from the ancient Korean word for 'gift,' is the innovative cuisine that husband and wife team - Chef Junghyun and manager Ellia Park, hope to deliver to the world using New York City as their stage. Atomix, a follow-up to their well-loved firstborn Atoboy, is a place where guests can really dive deep into Chef Park’s cuisine through a tasting menu that is inspired by Korean traditions and technique.

ld_json.name: Oriole
ld_json.description:
Oriole is a restaurant hidden down an alley-like street in Chicago’s West Loop neighborhood, offering an extended tasting menu presented by Executive Chef & Owner Noah Sandoval.   

Never bending to industry trends, the dishes and service at Oriole give guests a thought-provoking and interactive experience, where the diner is the true focus of the meal.

ld_json.name: Alinea
ld_json.description: Alinea has been universally praised for its innovative approach to modernist cuisine. It has been named the Best Restaurant in the World by Elite Traveler, the Best Restaurant in North America by The World’s 50 Best Restaurants, and the Best Restaurant in the U.S. by Gourmet and Business Insider. It is one of only 14 restaurants in the U.S. to earn the coveted Michelin 3-Star rating.

Lagasse, who’s definitely kicking it up a notch with an all-stops-out nightly tasting menu that might range from smoked salmon cheesecake with Petrossian caviar to lobster gumbo, to good old banana cream pie.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Opened in 1990, Emeril’s is Chef Emeril Lagasse’s acclaimed flagship restaurant located in the Warehouse District in New Orleans. Now helmed by his son E.J. Lagasse, the menu features a refined and elegant approach to Louisiana cuisine, rooted in Chef Emeril’s signature bold flavors. Known for elevated and warm hospitality, Chef E.J. and his team draw inspiration from the bounty of Louisiana produce from the most dedicated farmers, fishermen and purveyors to craft a menu that tells a story through food and nature.

Two Michelin Stars

A member of Relais & Chateaux

5 Diamonds, AAA, 2024

New Talent of the Year Award, La Liste 2024

Grand Award, Wine Spectator 2024

Top 1000 Restaurants, La Liste 2024

need_to_know.body:
Emeril's offers a tasting menu that features both classic Emeril's dishes along with seasonal selections.  To view the full tasting menu please visit us at Emerilsrestaurant.com

We attempt to accommodate any allergies, dietary restrictions or aversions for our guests whenever possible. Please notify us of any dietary needs at least 48 hours prior to your reservation, or we may not be able to accommodate. Please note, we are currently unable to offer menus that are vegan, vegetarian, allium-free, or completely free of gluten, nightshades, dairy, soy, seafood, or mushrooms.

We encourage dressing up for this special night. Jackets are recommended, collared shirts required for gentleman. Hats, t-shirts, shorts, athletic wear and flip-flops are not permitted.

Emeril's welcomes diners over the age of 8.

ld_json.name: Restaurant Pearl Morissette
ld_json.description:
Located in the Niagara region of Southern Ontario, an hour drive southwest of Toronto, Restaurant Pearl Morissette reflects the European ideal of destination dining in the heart of agriculture. Offering an ambitious fine dining experience featuring an ever-changing prix fixe menu composed of the highest quality ingredients of the region, inspired by seasonal French cooking.

The indoor dining room sits on the top floor of Pearl Morissette Estate Winery on the 42-acre property. With scenery through floor-to-ceiling windows of the surrounding regenerative farm, annual vegetable & flower garden, a whimsical perennial & herb plot, and local peach orchard. 

Founded on a holistic approach of regenerative practices and processes. Working with regional purveyors, the food and wine are a reflection of the local ecosystem and the land inhabited. RPM acknowledges that the treaty land, Niagara / Land of First Nations, which it benefits from, is situated on the traditional territory of the Hatiwendaronk, the Haudenosaunee, and the Anishinaabe, including the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation. This territory is covered by the Upper Canada Treaties and is within the land protected by the Dish With One Spoon Wampum Agreement.

ld_json.name: Enclos
ld_json.description:
Enclos, located in the heart of Sonoma, is a refined yet welcoming restaurant led by Chef Brian Limoges, whose culinary approach combines innovative techniques with a deep respect for seasonal, locally-sourced ingredients. Chef Limoges brings his refined French training and global experience to every dish, crafting a menu that celebrates California’s abundant produce, sustainable meats, and the region’s rich agricultural bounty. The restaurant’s intimate, modern space invites guests to experience an elevated dining experience with thoughtfully composed dishes that highlight the best of Sonoma's flavors.

We are happy to accommodate dietary needs within the limitations of our set menu and kitchen. To ensure the best possible experience, we kindly ask that all dietary restrictions be shared with us at least 72 hours in advance of your reservation. We are unable to accommodate last-minute or unexpected dietary needs without adequate notice.

Please see below for details on what we can and cannot accommodate:

•	Vegetarian: We are pleased to offer a thoughtfully prepared vegetarian menu with advance notice.

•	Allium Sensitivity: We can accommodate requests to avoid alliums in solid form (e.g., onions, garlic), while still allowing their use in stocks or as subtle background flavors. We cannot offer a fully allium-free experience.

•	Vegan Diets: Due to the nature of our preparations and ingredients, we are unable to accommodate a fully vegan menu.

•      Egg Allergy: Eggs play a foundational role in many of our preparations, and as a result, we’re unable to safely accommodate guests with a severe egg allergy.

•	Celiac & Gluten Sensitivity: We want to be fully transparent—due to the nature of our kitchen and menu, trace amounts of gluten are present throughout the experience. As such, we cannot guarantee a gluten-free or celiac-safe meal.

•	Dairy: We can accommodate guests who are comfortable with minimal dairy (e.g., butter, cream, or milk used sparingly), but we are unable to provide a completely dairy-free menu.

•	Seaweed Sensitivity: Seaweed is an essential ingredient in several components of our menu—particularly broths and dishes like our chowder and tuna course. While we can adjust or substitute certain courses (including vegetarian alternatives), we are unable to eliminate seaweed entirely.

•	Special Menus (e.g., New Year’s Eve, Valentine’s Day): Due to the nature of these offerings, we are unable to accommodate dietary restrictions during special menu events.

If you have other dietary concerns, we encourage you to reach out in advance. We will do our best to assist within the scope of our culinary program and greatly appreciate your understanding.

The restaurant, operated by Giancarlo Paterlini and Executive Chef Suzette Gresham, has been heralded for its cuisine, wine, and service. Keeping ahead of the ever-changing dining scene in San Francisco, Acquerello showcases its brightest young talent in the kitchen as well as with its wine program. “At Acquerello, we believe that refined luxury is always in style. Our desire is to provide our guests an experience of classic and contemporary Italian tastes in an elegant dining atmosphere.” Acquerello has received countless awards, including two Michelin stars, and the Wine Spectator Grand Award from 2012 to 2020.

review.reviewBody: I always have such a lovely experience here. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the service is consistently attentive and thoughtful. This has become one of my favorite places to celebrate special moments, and I often come here with friends for our anniversaries. The chef’s seasonal creations always impress me and bring something new to look forward to every time. It always feels a little more meaningful every time I visit. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a cozy and memorable dining experience.

Very special experience. Definitely an A.

The music, full plays of three vinyl albums, made the dinner significantly more fun.

The incremental charges for the truffles and beef were not value additive and I would not choose those again.
What an outstanding dining experience. The chef was amazing and the service was impeccable. Fantastic food and an amazing restaurant!

The food, service, presentations, sense of intimacy, and attention to detail were all outstanding, but the pièce de résistance was the turntable playing the chef’s vinyls throughout dinner. It was such a delight to see them take turns switching the albums. The anticipation of which one was next was as exciting as seeing what dish was coming. It was an absolutely sublime experience. Bravo!

Melisse is a different level of dining.  Only a small group of tables facing the kitchen with very personalized service of highly trained, friendly staff who care about each interaction.  Although not “stiff” they could still be more relaxed in such an intimate setting.  Artistically designed and presented, it is hard to imagine a more elevated experience.  When my wife asked about a specific design of a bowl the chef came out and personally found the information and discuss the serving objects.  Vintage R&R LPs are curated and played while dining. This is not a loud boisterous crowd, everyone (staff and patrons) is involved with their food and the experience (except the couple at the next table taking selfies).   When the bill comes… well … remember this is also an elevated experience.

The food was very creative and tasteful, nothing that we have had in the past in a Michelin star restaurant. We expected something more for the anniversary than a note, since it was a 3rd year anniversary, we wanted the note to say that but other than that, the service was excellent. The 4% charge seemed unnecessary, we don't mind paying an additional amount but it would have been better to add it to the food amount and not as a service for the kitchen and staff when we do give 20% tip regularly. The music was excellent and the pieces of art that surrounded the tables as well. We have been to Citrin and thought the room was going to be claustrophobic but it was not, it seemed as we were transported somewhere else, a very cool spot where magic happened.

Dinner at Melisse was even better than expected. The food was exquisite and prepared by the four chefs in the open kitchen. Watching them was part of the fun. If I could afford it I would do it again. Staff was wonderful and I felt like all of the diners should stand up and applaud at the end of the sumptuous meal. What a treat!
Still one of the best restaurant experiences in California - comparable to most Michelin 3 Star restaurants in my opinion, and much more relaxed and intimate for my personal tastes.

It was beautiful! I loved the rock ‘n’ roll music that they played. The service was impeccable, and the food was absolutely fabulous. Unique flavors burst in your mouth. Each course was so beautifully organized, and I love the sequence of the meals.￼

Melisse strives to make the entire dining experience exceptional from the moment you’re welcomed into their intimate space.  Food and presentation are breathtaking and amazing. Some of the most unique flavor sensations I’ve ever experienced. Each course is a delight!  Cocktails and wine are above par. Service is friendly, not stuffy and your every need is looked after.  Love the playlist too !
Chef Josiah has created a very unique experience that feels like you’re dining in his home with fresh ingredients from his garden.

review.reviewBody: Had the tasting menu with the prestige wine pairing . Fantastic. What an experience. Strongly recommend

The food was lovely, the general manager was warm and friendly and we really enjoyed getting to know our bartender-sommelier. Everything was going fine until we were done with the meal. Our table had been cleared and we sat there and waited for 30 minutes for our bill to come so we could head back to our hotel. We kept trying to wave someone down, make eye contact and we kept getting ignored, it took us almost 40 minutes to get our bill and be able to leave.
Good to experience the new season menu. My favourite dish was the scallops starter. Attentive service. A lovely experience.
The evening to celebrate a significant birthday was really nice and the food was perfect
Attentive, professional staff.  But… excruciatingly long wait between some of the later courses (20+ min more than twice) kind of killed it for us
An unforgettable experience, I will definitely be back!
Very good service , place was clean + great selection of non-alcoholic wines and drinks
Wonderful and exceptional food fit for a King served with consummate skill 5 Stars
While the tasting was pleasant, it didn’t quite leave a lasting impression or inspire a return visit.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was great, and the food was delicious. I had the 4-course lunch, but I was a bit disappointed that I could only choose two out of the four types of bread offered. It would have been better if they served all four varieties.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Glovers Alley?

ld_json.name: Bastible
ld_json.description: Bastible is located just a short stroll from the landmark St Patricks Cathedral in the vibrant postcode of Dublin 8.The restaurant overlooks the junction of Clanbrassil Street and South Circular Road in what was once the old Jewish quarter of Portobello.Chef Killian Walsh leads the kitchen team and creates seasonal tasting menus using his varied and considerable industry experience. Bastible was awarded a coveted Michelin Star in 2022 and proudly retains it today.Bastible's atmosphere is relaxed and inclusive. There is no required dress code and we pride ourselves on friendly and knowledgable service.We look forward to seeing you at Bastible soon.

review.reviewBody: We had a brilliant lunch celebrating a 70th birthday. Bastible staff looked after us so well, from wine selection, translating the menu on the spot and ending with a birthday treat.
One of the best service and food and had. From start to finish all the staff were very kind and the tasting menu is outstanding, specially the deserts.
Had an amazing experience here, the service was excellent and every item on the tasting menu was so creative. I will definitely be back

Felt taken care of from start to finish. The wines, food, service and pacing of the tasting were 12/10 impeccable. Bastible sets the standard for my first visit to Ireland of how deliciously innovative modern Irish cuisine can be and the relaxed atmosphere let me enjoy each flavor to the fullest. Hope to visit again in the future! Worth the flight from Denver

A spectacular experience. Every dish was delicious, with an incredible mix of textures and flavors. The service was excellent as well — everyone was very kind and attentive at all times. We ordered a bottle of wine for dinner, which made the experience even better. I loved it. Highly recommended.

Outstanding attention to detail, and each course was an explosion of flavor and texture. The service was on point - special thanks to Dan. Intimate with just the right amount of tables/noise to have a fun vibe as well. We had 3 vegetarian guests who thoroughly enjoyed their menu as well.
Only limitation is the drink link as it is only wine-centric. Works out ok in the end for the pairings but a few mainstay cocktails would be a good addition.

Would definitely recommend to friends and family who travel to Dublin and Bastible deserves the Michelin star they received.

We paid 300 for a bottle of red Italian wine. I’m
Sorry I didn’t raise it at the time.

The wine was just okay

Scallops were very well cooked, compliments to the chef. Chawanmushi was split/broken and way too salty. Saving grace was that fermented corn in the dish is very nice, give us more! It will make the dish a lot more balanced. Cod was a very smart dish, loved the buttermilk foam and hibiscus powder, and licorice was very creative. Razor clam: needs horseradish to be more forward, couldn’t taste it, while grapefruit foam was way too acidic.
Really amazing food. Bit of a delay before the “main” course, but we didn’t mind too much. Servers were very attentive. A lovely experience.
Beautiful food in a beautiful setting. I had the vegetarian menu as I am allergic to fish, and it was incredible. Great service, great champagne, great night.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Bastible is an excellent choice for a date night. Guests frequently praise the relaxed, cosy-yet-elegant atmosphere, attentive service and creative tasting menu, which many people book for anniversaries and special occasions. Expect a multi-course tasting experience with wine pairings, warm service and a comfortable, unfussy vibe, great for an intimate celebration. Consider an earlier seating if you prefer a quieter table.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant kid-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Families do dine at Bastible and guests have brought children for special occasions, but remember it’s a tasting‑menu restaurant with multiple courses and a quieter, intimate layout. It suits older children and teens better; for younger kids consider an early seating and call ahead to discuss menu flexibility.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ambience is relaxed, warm and unpretentious with a modern-minimalist feel, cosy rather than formal. Guests describe it as lively and friendly, with knowledgeable, enthusiastic staff and an open-kitchen buzz. It’s casual‑elegant: high-quality dining without stiffness, though it can get noisy when busy.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have accessible or family-friendly seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bastible welcomes families and many guests bring older children or celebrate milestones with younger family members. The space is intimate with some high stools and close‑set tables, so comfort may vary, a few guests mentioned high stools without backs. If you need accessible seating or specific family arrangements, call ahead so the team can advise and try to accommodate you.

mainEntity.name: What is this restaurant's stand-out or favorite dish?

acceptedAnswer.text: There isn’t a single fixed ‘signature’ dish, Bastible is best known for its seasonal tasting courses. Guests frequently praise scallops (and seafood dishes), the mushroom custard, pea ravioli, and game dishes like pigeon or sika deer. Standouts change with the seasonal menu, so expect imaginative Irish‑inspired plates that vary throughout the year.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Busiest: weekend evenings (Wed–Sat service with Saturday often busy) and late seatings, guests note lively, sometimes noisy nights. Quietest: earlier midweek seatings (the 17:30 service) or Saturday lunch can feel calmer. Booking earlier in the evening typically gives a slightly more relaxed experience.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Bastible?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casual dress is perfectly fine, Bastible promotes a relaxed and inclusive atmosphere with no required formal dress code. Guests often dress smart‑casual for a tasting‑menu evening, but you won’t need formal wear.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have vegan/vegetarian, gluten-free or other dietary options?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Bastible is accommodating with dietary needs. Guests frequently praise the vegetarian and plant‑based tasting menus and report that staff adapt dishes and provide gluten‑free options when asked. Notify the restaurant at booking so the kitchen can prepare an excellent tailored tasting experience.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any specials deals or experiences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bastible’s main offering is its seasonal tasting menu and curated wine pairings, the experience itself is the highlight rather than discount deals. Guests frequently book tasting menus for special occasions (birthdays, anniversaries, proposals); if you’re planning something special, note it when booking and the team will often help personalise the experience.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have a waiting list for bookings or at busy periods?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bastible is small and popular, so evenings fill up rapidly, many guests recommend booking in advance. The listings don’t explicitly state a waiting list, so if your preferred time is taken contact the restaurant directly to ask about cancellations or a wait list.

mainEntity.name: What are the portion sizes like at this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portions are those you’d expect from a tasting‑menu restaurant: small, carefully composed courses rather than large plated mains. Many guests love the balance and creativity, though several comment the tasting portions can feel light for the price, some chose wine pairings and still wanted a bit more food. If you prefer a heartier meal, consider a full wine pairing or asking staff for guidance when booking.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Bastible?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a lively, full experience choose an evening booking (Wed–Sat). If you prefer a slightly quieter service, aim for an earlier 17:30 seating midweek or the Saturday lunch service. Bastible is popular, so booking in advance is recommended, later evening seatings can be busier and noisier.

mainEntity.name: Can I make any special requests before I arrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, guests routinely request dietary changes and celebrations in advance, and the team is happy to help. Reviews note personalised attention for birthdays, engagements and dietary restrictions; call or include notes with your booking so Bastible can prepare and make your visit special.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to Bastible?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you want a slightly quieter experience, choose a midweek evening (Wednesday or Thursday) or the Saturday lunch service. Weekend evenings are lively and popular, excellent if you enjoy a buzzy atmosphere, but they tend to be the busiest times.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant serve alcohol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Bastible offers alcohol, with a strong emphasis on wine. Guests regularly recommend the wine pairings and praise the knowledgeable sommelier; cocktails and bottles are also available. A few guests noted limited beer options, so if you prefer craft beer or specific drinks it’s worth checking ahead or asking when you arrive.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Bastible holds a Michelin star. The restaurant was awarded a Michelin 1 Star in 2022 and continues to be celebrated by guests for its high-quality tasting menus and service.

need_to_know.body:

ld_json.name: Masseria
ld_json.description:
Chef Nicholas Stefanelli approaches hosting guests in his restaurant as more of a lifestyle than a profession, taking the pretense out of fine dining in favor of heartfelt hospitality and honest cooking. Featuring an open-air courtyard with relaxed seating, a covered pergola seating area, and an indoor sala with a view of the seafoam green-tiled open kitchen, Masseria, brings together the rustic but welcoming aesthetic of an Italian country estate, the industrial grit of the Union Market district.

Masseria features 3 dining experiences: a special 8-course Chef's Tasting Menu at our Chef's Table, Chef's Counter, Sala, and Veranda tables. Our 4-course Gustare and La Cucina menus are available at our Bar, Sala, and Veranda. 

An a la Carte menu is available at the bar upon request for walk-in guests only. Seats at the bar are not reserved for a la carte. 

Reservations are available a month in advance. Reservations are strongly encouraged due to limited seating availability.

content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Plant-focused Oyster Oyster is driven by making sustainability a priority in restaurants. Award-winning Chef Rob Rubba and Team create a seasonal menu that highlights the bounty of the Mid-Atlantic with local farms and producers who share their ethos, capturing the essence of each season. The beverage program echoes that same philosophy by curating a list of responsibly sourced wine and beer, while also offering juice pairings made by the culinary team to provide a non-alcoholic experience.

need_to_know.body:
Our menu utilizes soy, mushrooms, seeds, alliums, and nightshades, which will not be omitted from our current menu. 

We can accommodate most common allergies with prior notice. 

Reach out to hello@oysteroysterdc.com for more information regarding dietary restrictions.

A 22% service charge is added to the cost of your meal. This fee goes directly to all hourly team members.

content.body: Aaron Silverman's ode to fine dining upends everything you thought you knew about it. At Pineapple and Pearls, you're cordially invited to experience one of the best, and most memorable parties you've ever been to, that also just happens to have some incredible food.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Our standard menu is priced at $350 in the Dining Room and at the Chef's Counter (effective May 1, 2026, the menu price will increase to $360 per person). Fancy cocktails and amazing wines will be offered a la carte. The menu price is not inclusive of DC tax (10%) and service charge (22%). The service charge is not a tip, and is used to help cover the base wages and benefits of staff. Please note that we are a no tipping establishment.
In order to ensure the proper planning of your evening, please allow for 2.5 hours.

We can accommodate almost all allergies and dietary restrictions with advance notice. Just email us at reservations@pineappleandpearls.com and we will be happy to customize a menu for you.
P.S. We heart single diners!

We always reserve seats at our Chef’s Counter for single diners every night but if you prefer a table or the bar, please reach out to us at reservations@pineappleandpearls.com.

To host a private event with us, please reach out to events@rosesrestaurantgroup.com.
Cancellations and modifications to reservations will only be accepted in advance of 30 days of the reservation date.

need_to_know.body:
Get ready for a big night out! This is your excuse to put on your best outfit and show off.

Pineapple and Pearls is no longer a traditional fine dining restaurant. Say goodbye to the "four hour tasting parade to the chef". Say hello to a new kind of experience where pleasure is valued over perfection.

THIS IS A PARTY. Every night.

You just happen to get an amazing meal while you are here.

We are open Wednesday through Saturday. Our menu is designed as an exciting four course (large portioned) menu with choices for each course.

We do not have a dress code. But...if we did, it would be "fancy". Something along the lines of emerald green tuxedo dinner jackets and gold sequin dresses (or your best New Year’s Eve outfit).

content.body: Rethink your concept of fish in two hours and 20 bites at Sushi Nakazawa. At a sleek, minimalist counter, chef Daisuke Nakazawa, of Jiro Dreams of Sushi fame, prepares a sushi omakase unlike any other. Accompany the outstanding fish with the sake pairing, and you’ll be dreaming of sushi in no time.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Sushi Nakazawa is a critically-acclaimed omakase destination, born in New York City, from prominent restaurateur Alessandro Borgognone. Chef Daisuke Nakazawa is at the helm, and he sources ingredients both domestically and internationally to craft an Edomae-style tasting menu each night. A modern design, influenced by both east and west, sets the scene.

need_to_know.body:
Reservations become available at 12:00pm EST, 14 days in advance of a specific date.

Sushi Nakazawa serves Chef Nakazawa's Omakase menu exclusively. We do not offer A La Carte dining. We cannot accept requests for Sashimi, a Vegetarian menu, or a Soy Allergy. 

The starting price of the Omakase is $190.00 at the Sushi Counter and $160.00 in the Dining Room. Guests joining us at our Sushi Counter will be served by a chef directly. Guests joining us in our Dining Room will have the Omakase menu served in approximately 7 courses, each consisting of different flights of Nigiri-sushi. 

Dress Code: We ask our guests to respect the restaurant’s dress code. We ask for no hats, no shorts, no sweatpants/athletic wear, no tank tops, or sandals/flip flops while you dine with us. Jackets are not required. 

Multiple Reservations: All guests that book multiple reservations under their account will have their reservations automatically cancelled without notice.

Cancellation Policy: We have a strict 48-hour cancellation/change policy. Any cancellation or decrease in guest count within 48 hours may result in the credit card on file being charged the price of the omakase for every guest in the party. 

Please check with the restaurant if you have any questions. We look forward to hosting you soon.

content.body: The latest and greatest from chef Daniel Boulud extols the fruits of both land and sea in a stunning floral-edged oasis that will instantly make you forget you’re in Midtown. (10,000 pounds of lush black olive trees imported from Florida will certainly do the trick.) Named in homage to Henri Soulé’s iconic restaurant, which defined the culture of haute French dining in Gotham as far back as 1941, Le Pavillon celebrates the tradition of the grand restaurant, making it ideal for posh dining both day and night.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Renowned Chef Daniel Boulud introduces Le Pavillon, a unique culinary oasis in the heart of midtown Manhattan that is both comfortable and inviting with a refined elegance. The menu at Le Pavillon highlights vegetable-forward and seafood-centric dishes, an extension from Chef Daniel’s other restaurants which celebrate New York with a more contemporary French-American spirit.

content.body:
PLEASE READ BEFORE BOOKING: 

Please note that the full price of the tasting menu, $285 per person, will be charged per guest if a reservation is cancelled with less than one week's notice. Guests may transfer ownership of a reservation to a guest of their choosing should they not be able to attend their dinner. Please arrive on time. Tables will be held for a 15 minutes grace period before the cancellation fee is applied. Given this is a 12-course tasting menu, we ask that you kindly allocate 2.5 hours - 3 hours to your dining experience. 

WE ARE UNABLE TO ACCOMMODATE: DAIRY FREE, VEGAN, VEGETARIAN, NO SESAME, and/or NO SEAFOOD REQUESTS.

No small children are allowed in the restaurant - we ask that should you wish to bring a child of age that they participate in the entire tasting menu along with the rest of the party.

Guests are encouraged to dress smart casual. Shorts, athletic wear, flip flops, slides and baseball hats are not permitted.

Huso is located within the Marky’s Caviar retail shop at 323A Greenwich Street, at the intersection of Greenwich St. and Duane St. in the heart of Tribeca, NYC. Please note there is garage parking nearby, however, the 1, 2, and 3 trains are conveniently located next door. No Valet Parking.
content.name: need_to_know

content.body:
Tucked away within Marky's Caviar retail shop in the heart of Tribeca, One MICHELIN Star Huso invites you on a culinary journey that marries seasonal ingredients with the elegance of caviar, all under the masterful guidance of Executive Chef Buddha Lo. Originally opened within Marky’s Caviar on Madison Ave. in 2019, Huso quickly became a hidden gem, offering an intimate 12-seat experience where every dish was meticulously crafted in a humble kitchen, consisting of just a convection oven and stovetop. The restaurant’s Michelin-plated acclaim, coupled with Chef Lo’s rise as the winner of Top Chef Season 19 and Top Chef World All Stars, sparked an overwhelming demand, propelling our move to Tribeca.

Here, in our new home, Chef Lo and his team elevate their seasonal tasting menus to new heights, harnessing the power of a full-service kitchen and direct access to some of the finest gourmet ingredients and caviar. In our 26-seat dining room, evenings are an exploration of flavor, where every course reflects the chef’s innovative take on the season’s finest produce coupled with caviar-inspired plates. For intimate gatherings, we recommend parties of 1-4 be seated within our dining room, while larger groups can enjoy an exclusive experience downstairs, seated at the Chef's Table —an atmospheric space nestled within the very belly of the kitchen, accommodating up to 8 guests. Given this is a 12-course tasting menu, we ask that you kindly allocate 2.5 hours - 3 hours to your dining experience. 

To inquire about private dining or restaurant buyouts, please contact us directly at huso@husony.com

content.body: Contra alumnus Fidel Caballero is behind this exciting Mexican restaurant in the heart of Chinatown where you can expect tasting menus, a chef’s counter, and a standout à la carte menu featuring fiercely regional Northern Mexican ingredients and techniques drawn from around the globe. Don’t sleep on the drinks, either, many of which feature sotol and other agave-based spirits you may or may not have had before.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Corima is a Progressive Mexican restaurant that combines flavors from Chef Fidel Caballero’s upbringing in the north of Mexico, global influence from his travels, and a strong focus on local and seasonal cooking. Corima — which translates to “circle of sharing” — highlights ingredients and techniques from the northern states of Mexico alongside Japanese, Chinese, and Spanish flavors to bring a unique, Progressive Mexican cuisine to New York City. 

Chef Caballero hails from the border towns of Ciudad Juárez, MX and El Paso, TX. He has spent the last fifteen years cooking around the world from spending time in Basque Country with the great Martin Berasategui*** to sous chef at Contra* in New York, as well as Shanghai, to name a few. 

The beverage menu at Corima pays homage to the Northern region’s rich heritage, focusing on Mexican spirits such as Sotol, as an ode to the Chihuahuan Desert, along with natural wines from the Guadalupe Valley.

need_to_know.body: Chef's Counter and Tasting Menu reservations require full party participation for our $140 tasting menu. Unfortunately, we are unable to accommodate any allergies or dietary restrictions in our tasting menu at this time. Tasting Menu and Chef's Counter dining is a 2 hour and 15 minute experience but please feel free to continue the evening at our bar following the meal.  A La Carte reservations are available each day for the front of the restaurant as well as bar seating. Limited bar seats will be available for walk ins each evening.

why_we_like_it.body: Contra alumnus Fidel Caballero is behind this exciting Mexican restaurant in the heart of Chinatown where you can expect tasting menus, a chef’s counter, and a standout à la carte menu featuring fiercely regional Northern Mexican ingredients and techniques drawn from around the globe. Don’t sleep on the drinks, either, many of which feature sotol and other agave-based spirits you may or may not have had before.

en-us: Corima will offer multiple dining experiences each evening. A $140, eight to twelve course tasting menu will highlight Chef Fidel's food with an optional beverage pairing to accompany. Limited seating will be available each evening at the six seat chef's counter that will give an intimate view of the open kitchen during dinner services. Full service, a la carte dining will be available at the front of the restaurant and at the bar.

content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: JUA (joo-ah) is one-of-a-kind Korean wood-fire restaurant by chef Hoyoung Kim. Chef Kim is a former executive chef of two-Michelin-starred Jungsik in Tribeca. JUA is the chef's gift to his firstborn daughter Jua whose name signifies "joie" in French. The restaurant utilizes a variety of wood-fire techniques to present an original 7 course tasting menu.

need_to_know.body:
We are offering a seven-course tasting menu for $150.
Reservations are released daily at midnight, three weeks in advance.
Two seating times per night at 6:00pm or 8:30pm (Tues-Sun).
*Closed Mondays.

Please note that we are unable to accommodate vegan, vegetarian, dairy-free, no seafood, no allium, no soy, no sesame and gluten-free requests. For all other dietary needs, please contact us at info@juanyc.com

Due to limits on our seating capacity and to ensure ample time to cleaning and sanitizing, we kindly ask all guests to honor a two-hour time limit.

To avoid a fee of $70 per guest, please ensure any change or cancellation to your reservation is made at least 12 hours prior to your scheduled time.

Phone calls will be answered only between 2pm and 5pm.
Please email us at info@juanyc.com for the fastest response.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Tempura Matsui is an excellent choice for a special date night. The intimate, minimalist dining room and counter seating create a quietly romantic atmosphere, and the tempura omakase is designed as a thoughtful, multi-course experience. Expect attentive, Japanese-style hospitality and Michelin-starred execution; it’s best for celebrations or a memorable evening rather than a quick meal. Note the Omakase Dinner is a fixed experience (priced at $295 per guest) and reservations fill up, so book in advance.

mainEntity.name: What are the portion sizes like at this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portions follow an omakase format, you’ll get a sequence of many small, carefully timed courses rather than large single plates. Many guests find the meal generous and satisfying, though a few mentioned certain items (like the final rice don) could be larger if you want something heartier. Because it’s a tasting-style tempura omakase, plan for multiple delicate courses rather than big portions of any one dish.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have accessible or family-friendly seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partial, Tempura Matsui offers counter seating and a few private tables/booths and welcomes families for celebrations, but there’s no explicit public statement about ADA-accessible seating. Guests do bring teens and celebrate birthdays, and the staff have accommodated family requests. If you need accessible seating or specific family arrangements, call ahead so the team can confirm availability and help with seating.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Tempura Matsui?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a quieter, more relaxed experience, aim for a weekday dinner (early seating) or Friday lunch when offered. Counter seats are highly recommended for the full omakase interaction with the chefs. Weekends and special-occasion nights tend to be busiest, so booking the first seating or a weekday will usually feel more intimate and prompt.

mainEntity.name: What seating arrangements/rooms does this restaurant have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tempura Matsui is a small, focused space with counter seating where you can watch the chefs prepare tempura, plus a few private tables/booths. The counter is ideal for the omakase experience; there are limited seats overall, so reservations are recommended. The restaurant does not advertise a separate private dining room for large private events.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ambience is calm, elegant and distinctly Japanese, minimalist decor, quiet and intimate, and focused on the craft of tempura. Many guests say it feels like being transported to Japan, with warm, attentive hospitality and a refined, serene setting that suits special occasions and focused tasting meals.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Tempura Matsui?

acceptedAnswer.text: Business casual is the recommended dress code. Guests typically dress smartly for the Michelin-starred, fine-dining omakase experience, think neat, comfortable attire suitable for a special evening out.

mainEntity.name: Can I make any special requests before I arrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the team is used to handling special requests. Guests report the restaurant can accommodate allergies and dietary adjustments without sacrificing the menu’s quality, and the staff are attentive to celebration requests (e.g., birthday desserts). Call ahead when you reserve to discuss allergies, seating preferences, or celebratory arrangements.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant kid-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Families do dine here, and guests often celebrate birthdays with children, but this is a refined omakase experience best suited to older children or teens. There’s no kids’ menu, and the tasting format may be long for very young children. If you plan to bring younger kids, consider an early seating or reserve a table and call ahead to discuss accommodations.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have a waiting list for bookings or at busy periods?

acceptedAnswer.text: The restaurant doesn’t publicly advertise a formal waitlist, but seatings are limited and in high demand. Reservations may be made up to one month in advance, so it’s best to book early. If you can’t find availability, call the restaurant, they may offer cancellations or advise on timing for new openings.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Busiest: weekend dinners and special-occasion nights (many guests celebrate birthdays and anniversaries). Quietest: weekday dinners and the Friday/Saturday lunch service tend to be less crowded; early seatings are generally calmer. Because seating is limited, even quieter times can feel intimate, so book ahead for your preferred time.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to Tempura Matsui?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a balance of availability and a relaxed atmosphere, a weekday evening (Tuesday–Thursday) is often the best choice. If you want lunch, Friday or Saturday noon is offered. Weekend dinners are popular for celebrations but can be busier and pricier in terms of demand, so aim for weekdays if you prefer a quieter experience.

mainEntity.name: How is Tempura Matsui restaurant rated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tempura Matsui is rated 4.9 stars by 712 OpenTable diners.

mainEntity.name: Is Tempura Matsui currently accepting reservations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can generally book this restaurant by choosing the date, time and party size on OpenTable.

content.body: Rethink your concept of fish in two hours and 20 bites at Sushi Nakazawa. At a sleek, minimalist counter, chef Daisuke Nakazawa, of Jiro Dreams of Sushi fame, prepares a sushi omakase unlike any other. Accompany the outstanding fish with the sake pairing, and you’ll be dreaming of sushi in no time.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Executive Chef Daisuke Nakazawa's Omakase menu features different fish and shellfish globally, with a focus on Japanese waters. Highlighting seasonality, Chef's "New York-mae" style Omakase offers both classic, and modern interpretations of Edo-mae style Nigiri. 

The Same Omakase service is offered at seats at the Sushi Counter, Lounge Counter, or tables in the Dining Room.

need_to_know.body:
Reservations become available at 12:00pm EST, 14 days in advance of a specific date.

Sushi Nakazawa serves Chef Daisuke Nakazawa's Omakase menu exclusively. We do not offer A La Carte dining. We cannot accept requests for Sashimi, Cooked Fish, or a Vegetarian Menu. The same Omakase Menu is served for the Sushi Counter, Lounge Counter, and Dining Room. 

The starting price of the Omakase for dinner service is $190.00 at the Sushi Counter and Lounge Counter, and $160.00 in the Dining Room. We offer a shorter Omakase for lunch service starting at $150.00.

Guests at the Sushi Counter and Lounge Counter will be served by a Chef directly. 

Guests joining us in our Dining Room will have the Omakase menu served in approximately 7 courses, each consisting with different flights of Nigiri-sushi.

Dress Code: We ask our guests to respect the restaurant’s dress code. We ask for no hats, no shorts, no sweatpants/athletic wear, no tank tops, or sandals/flip flops while you dine with us. Please refrain from wearing strong colognes or perfumes. Jackets are not required. 

Multiple Reservations: All guests that book multiple reservations under their account will have their reservations automatically cancelled without notice.

Please check with the restaurant if you have any questions. We look forward to hosting you soon.

ld_json.name: noda
ld_json.description:
noda is the reimagination of a traditional omakase built around the guest experience. Classically trained in edomae, Chef Shigeyuki Tsunoda has relocated from Ginza, Tokyo to bring his culinary philosophy to New York. He is supported by a team of sommeliers who oversee one of the most extensive Japanese whiskey collections and who have curated a wine, sake and cocktail program specifically for the meal. All guests are seated at noda's counter; an 800-pound piece of unfinished wood that is sanded daily and designed in the shape of a half-moon to allow Chef an up close and personal experience with each and every guest. We serve twice nightly at 5:45pm and 8:45pm and ask that you please arrive on time to enjoy the complete dining experience. 

For private events or parties larger than 4 guests, please email events@noda.nyc. 

We look forward to welcoming you soon.

content.body: There are simple pleasures in life, and one of them is slurping through a steaming bowl of Jeju Noodle Bar’s ramyun. The Korean slurp shop with a Michelin star is helmed by chef-owner Douglas Kim (Bouley, Per Se), who makes use of his fine-dining chops to bring South Korean comfort food to its purest and tastiest form. Expect flavor-rich broths and bouncy noodles, with a bevy of elegant pre-noodle bites.
content.name: why_we_like_it
content.title: Why We Like It

about.body: Jeju, meaning Skill and Ability, is the first and only Michelin Starred noodle restaurant in the World. Known for Korean Inspired Cuisine, Chefs focus is to provide guests with the highest quality ingredients possible in a casual and fun atmosphere.

need_to_know.body:
We are currently offering indoor dining for groups of 2 to 4 guests. All parties have a 1 hour 45 minute dining experience. We look forward to welcoming you! 

For Party size larger than 4 & general inquiries please email reservations@jejunoodlebar.com

Please note, we are unable to accommodate vegan, vegetarian, gluten free, no seafood, no meat, and no allium requests.
need_to_know.title: Need to Know

tagline.body: Each of the three soups is so carefully considered, so well harmonized, that Jeju’s menu really could end there. But Mr. Kim makes a handful of Korean-inspired appetizers, too, all more nuanced than what you’d find in a typical ramen-ya. —NY Times
