content.body: Experience the cuisine that made Daniel Boulud famous on the Upper East Side: At Café Boulud, cafe culture is celebrated through à la carte dishes with global influences, while at Maison Barnes, it's all about the elegant prix fixe menu that celebrates French culinary traditions in a plush and intimate setting.
content.name: why_we_like_it

content.body:
Location: The restaurant is located on East 63rd street between Park & Lexington Avenue.

The Experience: While walk-ins are welcomed in our Bar and Lounge, reservations are suggested to experience our Dining Areas. 

The Dining Room:
The Dining Room offers a luminous and spacious setting, where high vaulted ceilings and an abundance of natural light meet the vibrant energy of a chic Parisian brasserie. With its grand proportions and emerald velvet accents, it provides a sophisticated, high-energy environment.

Le Salon:
Le Salon offers an intimate and quiet setting defined by its hand-painted murals and cozy, jewel-toned banquettes. Evoking the classic charm of the Belle Époque, this room is ideal for guests looking for a more private, relaxed, and conversation-focused experience.

Private Gatherings and Large Groups: Beyond our main rooms, Café Boulud at Maison Barnes reveals a collection of unique private spaces designed for exceptional events. For parties of 9 or more, or to explore our private bookings, we invite you to contact our Events Manager, Olivia, at oboude@danielboulud.com or corpeventsintern@danielboulud.com.

Our team is available daily from 10am to 8pm at (212) 772 2600 to guide your experience. Should you reach us after hours, please leave a message with your name and phone number where you may be reached, and a member of our team will return your call within 24 hours.

Smart casual attire is recommended.
content.name: need_to_know

content.body:
Café Boulud at Maison Barnes represents a unique union between the world-renowned culinary artistry of Chef Daniel Boulud and the BARNES Group, the international leader in the French Art de Vivre. This singular destination harmonizes Chef Daniel’s celebrated cuisine with the Maison’s elevated perspective on design, architecture, and the pursuit of elegance in every detail.

Beyond our main rooms, Café Boulud at Maison Barnes reveals a collection of five unique private spaces, from the Film Center and the Cellier to our discrete lounge, all available for private booking. These versatile settings offer absolute exclusivity, accommodating gatherings from quiet, personal dinners to grand celebrations, each meticulously tailored to create extraordinary moments. We invite you to explore these private spaces on our website and contact our Events Manager, Olivia, at oboude@danielboulud.com or corpeventsintern@danielboulud.com to discuss availability and bespoke arrangements.

about.body:
Café Boulud at Maison Barnes represents a unique union between the world-renowned culinary artistry of Chef Daniel Boulud and the BARNES Group, the international leader in the French Art de Vivre. This singular destination harmonizes Chef Daniel’s celebrated cuisine with the Maison’s elevated perspective on design, architecture, and the pursuit of elegance in every detail.

Beyond our main rooms, Café Boulud at Maison Barnes reveals a collection of five unique private spaces, from the Film Center and the Cellier to our discrete lounge, all available for private booking. These versatile settings offer absolute exclusivity, accommodating gatherings from quiet, personal dinners to grand celebrations, each meticulously tailored to create extraordinary moments. We invite you to explore these private spaces on our website and contact our Events Manager, Olivia, at oboude@danielboulud.com or corpeventsintern@danielboulud.com to discuss availability and bespoke arrangements.

need_to_know.body:
Location: The restaurant is located on East 63rd street between Park & Lexington Avenue.

The Experience: While walk-ins are welcomed in our Bar and Lounge, reservations are suggested to experience our Dining Areas. 

The Dining Room:
The Dining Room offers a luminous and spacious setting, where high vaulted ceilings and an abundance of natural light meet the vibrant energy of a chic Parisian brasserie. With its grand proportions and emerald velvet accents, it provides a sophisticated, high-energy environment.

Le Salon:
Le Salon offers an intimate and quiet setting defined by its hand-painted murals and cozy, jewel-toned banquettes. Evoking the classic charm of the Belle Époque, this room is ideal for guests looking for a more private, relaxed, and conversation-focused experience.

Private Gatherings and Large Groups: Beyond our main rooms, Café Boulud at Maison Barnes reveals a collection of unique private spaces designed for exceptional events. For parties of 9 or more, or to explore our private bookings, we invite you to contact our Events Manager, Olivia, at oboude@danielboulud.com or corpeventsintern@danielboulud.com.

Our team is available daily from 10am to 8pm at (212) 772 2600 to guide your experience. Should you reach us after hours, please leave a message with your name and phone number where you may be reached, and a member of our team will return your call within 24 hours.

Smart casual attire is recommended.

content.body: A brasserie for the modern age, Francie is the glitzy labor of love of two industry vets. Housed in an old bank, Francie reimagines the usual suspects. You’re going to want to try the foie gras canelé, market salad, and the showstopping dry-aged crown of duck.
content.name: why_we_like_it

content.body:
Thank you for making a reservation to dine with us!  You are about to become part of the Francie family and we look forward to welcoming you.  If you need assistance, don't hesitate to call us.  Our direct line is (718) 218-7572.  We will hold your table for 15 minutes, so please call if you're running late.  We answer our phones starting at 2 p.m., Monday through Saturday.  Our availability changes often. Francie accepts walk-ins. Weeknights are more flexible than weekends.  Francie reserves the right to ask for the table back after 2 hours.
CANCELLATION POLICY:  Francie charges a $25 per person fee for late cancellation, rescheduling, decrease in party size, and/or no-show.  Please cancel or modify your booking at least 24 hours in advance to avoid the fee.
In the event of a Zombie Apocalypse, all late cancellations and no-shows will be forgiven.  Please barricade yourself in, and good luck. 
*Francie technically does not have a dress code but if you could kindly dress for success, we (and the other diners) would appreciate it.

*Our kitchen can accommodate most common food allergies, but as a general rule: the more complicated the allergy, the less chance we have to modify the menu.

*The Vault at FRANCIE is available for private dining for parties up to 12 guests.  A la carte dining is available for smaller groups when a party is not booked.
DETAILS:  When you dine at Francie, you do not dine in a bubble.  Please be respectful of other diners and refrain from using flash photography, bright lights, and laptops.  Our staff are here to serve but they are not stars in your social media feed. Please do not photograph or film them without permission.   Francie does not permit outside food, including cakes.  Our corkage fee is $90 per 750ml bottle, at one 750ml bottle per two persons (maximum of 2 bottles).
content.name: need_to_know

content.body: Francie is a Michelin-starred New York Brasserie with Italian and French influence.  Francie is located in a limestone-clad former bank building and has the convivial feel of a neighborhood gathering place. James Beard Nominated Chef-Owner Chris Cipollone and Pastry Chef Justin Binnie serve a seasonal menu inspired by European flavors and designed for flexibility:  bar snacks, shellfish, handmade pastas and the famous Crown Roast of Rohan Duck.  Save room for the last remaining cheese cart in NYC.  Wines from around the world and classic cocktail list are presented with a flourish of seamless hospitality.  Private Dining in The Vault, the former bank vault, is a memorable experience.

content.name: why_we_like_it
content.title: Why We Like It

about.body: Oxomoco is a Michelin Starred wood-fired Mexican restaurant from chef and restaurateur Justin Bazdarich (Speedy Romeo), housed in a foliage-filled, sun-drenched space in Greenpoint. The regionally agnostic cuisine sources influence from across the country (Yucatan, Baja, Oaxaca, Mexico City, etc.), proudly using organic, heirloom corn from Mexico to prepare house-made tortillas. An extensive mezcal and tequila list provides the perfect pairing.

need_to_know.body:
Recently, OXOMOCO experienced a fire within the kitchen. Thanks to the swift response of our dedicated team and the FDNY, the situation was quickly controlled and we are relieved to report that damage was limited to the kitchen ventilation system.

In the meantime, the Oxomoco team is proud to announce Otoño de Oxomoco. 

Our new seasonal pop-up, celebrating autumn's warmth, harvest, and transformation while we await the return of our wood-fired kitchen. 

New dishes, same spirit, inspired by Oxomoco: goddess of nature and change.

content.body: If you find yourself in FiDi, or New York, period, Crown Shy is a must. Within the walls of this art-deco skyscraper, you'll find the late James Kent's vision of New American dining, overdelivered every step of the way by a talented team of chefs. You only need to look at their pull-apart loaf, the creation of pastry chef Renata Ameni, — maybe the most talked-about bread of 2019. The wine list, Ameni’s desserts, and the perfect roast chicken are also unforgettable.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Crown Shy is the first solo project from the late Chef James Kent. Located on the ground floor of Art Deco masterpiece 70 Pine Street, the restaurant was awarded a Michelin star just six months after opening, as well as the highest score given by The Infatuation in 2019.

Lunch Service
Join us for lunch service starting October 9th Monday through Friday from 11:30 AM to 2:00 PM!

Chef's Family-Style Menu at The Nook
At Crown Shy's semi-private Nook area, we can accommodate 11-18 people maximum seated in the Nook. The restaurant would still be in service around you, but the Nook corner section would be dedicated to your group.

We can reserve the Nook for a large party either at 5:30/6 pm or at 8/8:30 pm, Sunday – Thursday evenings. We offer a family-style 4-course pre-fixe food menu for $145 per person, not including beverages and tax. All beverages are billed on consumption. There is an automatic 20% gratuity added for these bookings.


Large Parties 

Reservations for parties of 8 guests or more will be served a prix fixe family-style menu for $145 per guest.


Reservations are available 28 days in advance to book, and look out for new reservations released every day at 10 am EST.

need_to_know.body: Our bar has 14 seats that we exclusively use to accommodate walk-ins on a first-come, first-served basis. We reserve a portion of our dining room for walk-ins.

content.body: Hidden below a staircase within the One Vanderbilt skyscraper, Jōji reunites George Ruan and Wayne Cheng — two Masa vets who met at the prestigious sushi counter and became close friends. For their Michelin-starred omakase experience (backed by Daniel Boulud), expect the same reverence for fish, a playlist that spans Biggie to French rap, and a stellar wine and sake list.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: At Michelin-starred Jōji, the chefs and sommelier share the culinary stage to create a dining experience unlike any other. Nestled within a serene refuge in the heart of Midtown's iconic One Vanderbilt, the intimate dining room is infused with authentic Japanese character, designed with a deep reverence of nature to create a refined and serene dining experience that both inspires and delights. The traditional multi-course omakase experience, led by chefs and partners George Ruan and Wayne Cheng, is uniquely designed for each guest using only the finest seasonally available ingredients, paired with premium sake and fine wine. With dining operations overseen by Michelin-starred chef Daniel Boulud’s The Dinex Group, Jōji delivers a sophisticated, elegant culinary journey for every guest. Jōji has been awarded a prestigious Michelin star.

need_to_know.body:
Dining Options & Pricing:
At Jōji, both the Sushi Bar and Private Dining Room (PDR) offer a seasonal Omakase menu priced at $410 per guest during dinner, with lunch seating available at $295 per guest. Kindly note that effective May 1st, Jōji will be updating its menu pricing. Dinner will be offered at $450 per guest, and lunch at $325 per guest.

Lunch seating at Jōji is available at 12:30 pm from Wednesday to Saturday, while dinner seatings are at 5:45 pm and 8:30 pm from Tuesday to Saturday. Reservations are available 14 days in advance.

Dietary Restrictions:
With such care going into the creation of each dish, certain dietary restrictions will be difficult to  accommodate and we need to be informed of any specific requirements at least 48 hours in advance. Regrettably, we are unable to accommodate vegetarian, vegan, or diets that restrict raw fish. 

Location:
The entrance of the restaurant is located at the corner of 43rd and One Vanderbilt below street level in the 1 Vanderbilt building

Cancellation Policy:
Please be aware of our strict 48-hour cancellation policy, which incurs a non-refundable fee of $150 per guest for lunch, $200 per guest for dinner at the sushi counter, and $250 per guest for the private dining room. Cancellations and reductions in the size of the party made less than 48 hours before the reservation time will be subject to cancellation fees, with no exceptions.

For their Michelin-starred omakase experience (backed by Daniel Boulud), expect the same reverence for fish, a playlist that spans Biggie to French rap, and a stellar wine and sake list.

content.title: Why We Like It

about.body: The Four Horsemen is a Michelin-starred and James Beard Award-winning restaurant with a world-renowned natural wine list in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. As a New York pioneer in the natural wine movement that first took off in Europe, the list here is extensive, eclectic, thoughtful, and full of unique finds. The food offerings from Chef Nick Curtola are constantly evolving, and vary from snacks to large plates. All of it is served by a friendly and knowledgeable waitstaff that are passionate about wine and what to pair it with.

need_to_know.body:
Dinner is served every day from 5:30pm to 10:45pm
Lunch is served Friday through Sunday 11:00am to 3:30pm

We're a tiny place — if you are 15 minutes late for your reservation, your table will be given away to a waiting guest. For dinner reservations, there is a $25 per person cancellation fee for cancelling your dinner reservation after 12PM on the day of your reservation. For lunch, there is a $25 per person cancellation fee for cancelling after 8PM the day before to your reservation. 

The bar is available for walk-ins and serves our full menu. We prioritize guests joining us for a full meal, and bar seats are offered on a first-come, first-served basis. All members of your party must be present in order to be seated. Walk-ins are accepted until 15 minutes before the kitchen closes.

Due to limited capacity, reservation times are limited to 1h45 for parties of 2; 2h15 for parties of 3-5 and 2h45 for parties of 6. 

We reserve the right not to honor reservations that have been traded or sold.
need_to_know.title: Need to Know

about.body:
Chef Daniel Boulud’s renowned restaurant delights the senses with elegant ambiance, gracious service and delectable menus in Manhattan’s Upper East Side.
Since opening in 1993, Restaurant Daniel has earned its place among the pillars of New York City’s bustling dining scene, receiving numerous accolades for its refined European cuisine, world-class wine cellar and gracious hospitality.  The seasonal cuisine highlights modern interpretations of traditional French fine dining, with prix fixe and tasting menu options, plus an a la carte menu and exceptional cocktails in our bar and lounge.

need_to_know.body:

The Lounge at DANIEL offers an a la carte menu, a 3-course seasonal prix fixe menu, 5-course seasonal prix fixe menu, and a 7-course seasonal tasting menu. 

The dress code at DANIEL is formal.  Jackets are strongly suggested for gentlemen. Please note shorts, sandals, athletic wear and distressed jeans are not allowed.

No meal is ever exactly the same, and the four-course menu, served family-style, of course, changes daily.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Blue Hill New York opened in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village neighborhood in April of 2000. The restaurant has evolved over the last two decades, sourcing ingredients from Blue Hill Farm, the Barber family’s dairy in Great Barrington, MA; from the Stone Barns Center for Agriculture in Pocantico Hills, NY; as well as from farms within 250 miles of New York City. Family Meal began in the summer of 2021 and welcomes guests to a menuless dining experience of shared plates.

need_to_know.body:
Reservations for Family Meal are bookable 28 days in advance beginning at 12am.  We welcome parties of 2-9 in the Main Dining Room and Garden Room. The full experience is available at the bar for parties of 1-2. For groups larger than 9 guests, please submit an inquiry for private dining at our website. 

DINNER
• 7 days a week, 5:30pm-9:30pm
• 4 courses
• $145 per guest
• Optional Wine Progression: $95 per guest

SATURDAY AND SUNDAY LUNCH
• Every Saturday and Sunday, 11:30am-2:00pm
• 3 courses
• $85 per guest

- Menu prices are exclusive of beverage, tax and gratuity. 
- Most dietary restrictions can be accommodated with advanced notice. Please specify all allergies and restrictions in your reservation notes. 

PRIVATE DINING
The Garden Room is available for private events hosting up to 14 guests. The Main Dining Room may be reserved for a full buyout for up to 40 guests. Please visit our website to submit an event inquiry.

about.body:
Dirt Candy serves cutting edge vegetables with added flavor and no politics in this sleek and stylish restaurant showcasing colorful, pop-tastic dishes from award-winning chef, Amanda Cohen. Dirt Candy only offers a 5 course Tasting Menu for $110/per person excluding beverages and tax. 

-Reservations are available for dinner from 5:30-10:30pm Tuesday through Saturday.

-Reservations for parties of 1-5 persons are available to book online up to 30 days in advance to each calendar date. Reservations are released at Midnight EST. Larger group reservations are booked over the phone, please call 212.228.7732. 

-We only offer a 5 course Chef's Tasting Menu for $110 per person, inclusive of service, but excluding beverages and tax. There are no a la carte options available. All guests aged 6 years and older must participate in the tasting menu. 

- A vegan version of our menu is always available, however no other substitutions or modifications can be accommodated. A gluten, soy or allium free diet cannot be accommodated. 
For any questions regarding allergies or dietary restrictions, please call the restaurant at 212.228.7732. 

-We can hold reservations for up to 15 minutes.  If you are running late please call the restaurant. 

-A $50 per person cancellation fee will be charged for all no shows and any cancellations with less than 24 hours notice to the reservation time. 

- To ensure we are able to accommodate all of our guests, we kindly ask all guests to limit time at the table to 2 hours for parties of 1-2 and 2 hours and 15 minutes for parties of 3 or more.

content.body: When an Eleven Madison Park alum goes back to his Chinese roots, you get something like Tuome: A Michelin-starred haunt that lays on the umami in thrilling ways — quail arrives splattered in soy sauce, luscious noodles come slicked with snow crab and dashi butter, and the “pig out for two” is a sight to behold.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Tuome is an ingredient-driven contemporary American restaurant with Asian influences. The chef/owner behind it all is Thomas Chen, whose resume includes Eleven Madison Park and Jean-Georges. The menu, which evolves seasonally, showcases his classic culinary training and Asian influences from his upbringing. Some must gets are the crispy deviled eggs and snow crab noodles with dashi butter.

need_to_know.body:
We are open Tuesday-Saturday. Reservations are available 15 days in advance. 

If you are running late, please call the restaurant at (646) 833-7811. Incomplete parties or those more than fifteen minutes late may forfeit their reservation. If this occurs, we will do our best to seat your party after everyone has arrived. 

We look forward to having you and your party as our guests.

about.body: Torrisi is a Michelin-star concept conceived by Chef Rich Torrisi that, in many ways, is an ode to Little Italy, but also a culinary journey through Chef Torrisi’s neighborhood. As you taste the dishes on the menu, you can almost feel the moment you arrive in Chinatown, or traverse the lower east side, cross Mulberry Street and smell the Zeppoli during the Feast of San Gennaro. A New Yorker both by upbringing and in his soul, this is his love letter to the city with the panache of his classic French culinary training, and the passion of his Italian American heritage.

need_to_know.body:

Guests are encouraged to dress for the occasion. Any guest who does not appear sufficiently well-presented may be refused entry. No shorts, open-toed shoes, or tank tops. Athletic wear and baseball caps are kindly prohibited.

Please be aware that reservations and deposits are non-transferable. Deposits will be refunded if cancellations are made by 12:00 PM on the day of the dinner reservation or at least 12 hours prior to lunch reservations.

For modifications or cancellations of existing bookings, inquiries about dietary restrictions or allergies, or to arrange prepayments, please contact us at reservations@torrisinyc.com.

We reserve our bar seating for walk-in guests. We encourage guests to visit and enjoy dining at the bar!

Reservations for both lunch and dinner can be made exclusively through Resy up to 30 days in advance, starting at 10:00 AM EST.

content.body: After working together at Brooklyn Fare and Bar Uchū, friends and former high school classmates chef Samuel Clonts and restaurateur Raymond Trinh decided to venture out on their own. The result is Sixty Three Clinton, where a whimsical tasting menu is ruled by the seasons and pulls from their personal histories. Think a breakfast taco with an ajitama ramen egg, salsa verde, and smoked trout roe — a wink to their Southwest upbringing and years of Japanese cooking.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Our intimate, seasonal menu of modern American fare takes cues from Chef Sam Clonts’ time in some of New York City’s best kitchens; reflecting both his appreciation for local ingredients and a global approach. To drink, Raymond Trinh’s beverage team has crafted an eclectic wine list from old and new-world selections that satisfy a variety of tastes, available by the glass or bottle. For something stronger, a cocktail menu rooted in the American classics with modern tweaks celebrates locally produced spirits, infusions and tinctures.

Our restaurant offers a 10 seat bar room which also offers 6 coveted counter seats facing inside the kitchen. Our 40 seat dining room offers our full and intimate experience of our concept. All seating options offer the same 7 course tasting menu.

need_to_know.body:
Reservations open 21 days in advance at midnight. We do not allow walk-ins for dinner.

We are currently offering our seven course tasting menu at $130 per person.
We allot a 20-minute grace period for parties arriving for reservations.

****Corkage policy: $75.00 per 750 milliliters. This fee is waived if a bottled is purchased off our wine list during your meal.

Parties of 6 guests or more will be charged a 20% service charge

***We are only offering the tasting menu at this time and are reservation only. Due to the nature of the menu, we are unable to accommodate certain dietary restrictions. We cannot accommodate vegan diets, severe allium/herb/spice allergies, coconut allergies, eggs, or soy/soybean allergies. We can accommodate vegetarian diners if they consume dairy and eggs. If you are unsure about your dining needs, please email or call us to inquire.***

Cancellation policy is 48 hours at 5pm prior to the reservation. If cancellation occurs once this 48-hour window has passed, a fee of $130 per person is incurred. Thank you for your understanding!

ld_json.description:
🚫 Beware of Unauthorized Discount Offers
We do not authorize any group or third party to offer our dinner at a discounted price.
If you have purchased a discounted reservation from an unauthorized source, please be aware that it may not be honored.
We may request a photo ID to confirm the reservation name or your relationship to the reserver.
Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.

**Both experiences are gratuity included on the price paid through Tock only. Any and all purchases made at the restaurant are not gratuity included.**
 
icca features two different experiences, at our bar area, located in the front of the restaurant is our Italian Kappo experience. The Omakase experience is hosted at our beautiful Omakase counter.

icca is an Omakase restaurant of intent and inspiration. An expression icca means to “open the flower of the heart” which shows the sensitivity and passion is our philosophy.

Each element speaks to the desire of Michelin Star awarded Sushi Chef Kazushige Suzuki, and his team who amazes and delights our guests.
Chef Kazu serves a seasonal and innovative Omakase menu that includes the finest fish air-shipped from the Toyosu Market in Japan. 

Our Bar hosts our Italian Kappo experience. Kappo Cuisine is a refined, multi-course dining experience that bridges the gap between the formal Kaiseki and casual Izakaya styles. Originating from the Edo Era, Kappo is a high-class cuisine celebrated for its counter seats, which grew in popularity during the Taishou and early Showa eras. Our Italian Kappo uses Italian and Japanese techniques to accentuate the flavor of the ingredients.

Seasonal ingredients are exclusively selected from Hokkaido, which highlights our signature Tokachi Herb Beef (N34). 


*Our menu includes raw and undercooked ingredients such as fish and shellfish, which may increase your risk of foodborne illness, especially if you are pregnant or have certain medical conditions.

*Our seasonal menu are currently not catered to vegetarian, vegan or gluten free options.

*Cancellations, reschedules or any changes to the reservation has to be made 72 hours prior to your reservation date. Any reservation that are past the 72 hour grace period are strictly non refundable with no exceptions. 

*Cancellations of parties of 4 guests or more must be made a week in advance. 

*For the safety of our guests, we reserve the right to cancel reservations if timely communication regarding allergies or dietary restrictions is unattainable. 

*Smoking, including e-cigarettes and vaping, is strictly prohibited on our premises. 
We also kindly ask that you refrain from wearing strong perfume or cologne, as it may interfere with the dining experience for yourself and other guests. 

Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.

Team icca

ld_json.name: Mako
ld_json.description:
Named after a species of shark known for its speed, precision, focus and instinct, Mako is renowned sushi chef B.K. Park's passion project, a highly-anticipated omakase located in Chicago's vibrant West Loop.

The set menu of up to 23 bite size pieces delivers a truly personal dining experience to the guest, with each bite exclusively prepared by the chef.  Showcasing unique cuts of fish and luxury ingredients highlighted by contemporary twists, this creative exploration is a celebration of Chef Park's expertise seeking out and serving the most pristine fish in the world.  Sophisticated beverage pairings complement the dishes and include thoughtfully chosen sakes, wines, Champagnes and dessert accompaniments. 

With only 22 seats (12 at a graphite walnut sushi bar), the intimate space reflects the beauty of organic patterns found in nature and sea life, with warm woods, a neutral palette and touches of blue and bronze tones. 

For parties 6 and up please contact us at info@makochicago.com

ld_json.name: Cariño
ld_json.description:
1. (afecto) love ⧫ affection

2. (apelativo) darling ⧫ honey 

Cariño is a Spanish word that refers to a feeling of fondness or love that a person has for someone or something.

This new concept is an immersive culinary journey offering a Latin-inspired tasting menu and taco omakase by Chef Norman Fenton. Each dish has been meticulously crafted to highlight the rich tapestry of flavors and ingredients found across Latin America. These unique combinations of traditional and contemporary techniques, promise to deliver an elevated dining experience that surprises and delights. 

Every little detail of Cariño's intimate setting is deeply personal and tells a story rooted in family and love of craft offering each guest an opportunity for a truly memorable dining experience .


A 25% service charge is applied to all dine-in checks in place of a tip to ensure our deserving staff members receive equitable pay and benefits. ALL gratuities and fees are included in this charge. Thank you for supporting fair compensation for industry employees.

ld_json.name: Topolobampo
ld_json.description:
Topolobampo: fine dining, authentic stories of Mexico

Sometimes a story of people and places, a time now distant, or even works of art that offer a glimpse into the uniqueness of Mexican life. Every story is deeply rooted in Mexico, and so is the food, though rarely does it resemble what you’d find in a traditional Mexican kitchen. 

Topolo presents Mexican cuisine through a contemporary, fine-dining lens, while bringing vibrant excitement and adventure that is sure to enchant even the most experienced culinary travelers.

Under the guidance of veteran Chef de Cuisine Meagan O’Connor and Pastry Chef Jennifer Enyart, both of whom have accompanied Chef Rick Bayless for decades as he has learned from cooks all over Mexico, Topolobampo is serving a six-course tasting menu that will delight and surprise, every time.

ld_json.name: Feld Restaurant
ld_json.description:
Feld is a relationship-to-table restaurant based in the heart of Chicago’s West Town. At Feld we create a  tasting menu that highlights the produce that we have carefully sourced from our network of growers, ranchers, fishermen, and dairy farmers. 

Feld is a demonstration in true seasonality, where the menu for each evening is created that morning in response to the produce available on that day.

A meal at Feld is not driven by a specific culture or cuisine, but by the produce of the moment and all the possibilities it allows us. The meal is prepared and plated directly in front of the guests, in the center of our dining room, with no separation except the table between guest and cooks.

We invite you to come dine with us, to let us welcome you into our home, and to experience the season through your plate as it can only be experienced on the night you dine.

content.body: The 20-course omakase menu at this Buckhead gem is the real deal. Chef Leonard Yu — who first brought his impeccable sushi to Atlanta with pop-ups at Silom Thai & Sushi Bar and Brush Sushi Izakaya — sources Koshihikari rice from Niigata and fish from Tokyo’s Toyosu market, and turns his ingredients into something truly exquisite.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Omakase Table by Leonard Yu is a two room omakase dining experience in Buckhead Landing. Our fish is sourced directly from Toyosu Fish Market in Tokyo to ensure the highest quality sushi possible. Chef Yu's seasonal tasting menu is curated daily based on availability and peak quality.

This chef's table experience consists of approximately 6 otsumami (Small Bites), 11 seasonal nigiri, atsuyaki tamago castella, temaki, and dessert.

need_to_know.body:
Unfortunately, specific dietary restrictions such as no rice, gluten-free, no raw fish, no shellfish, vegetarian or vegan cannot be accommodated. If you have any other serious allergies, please contact us.

For all parties, there is a 20% gratuity added to bookings/bills. 

Cancellations within 48 hours and no-shows will be charged 100% of the cost per person. Reduction in the number of guests in the party are subject to cancellation charge.

For guests interested in bringing their own beverages, please be aware that a corkage fee of $100 will be charged. This allows us to maintain the quality of service and experience during your stay. 

We are a reservation-driven and cashless restaurant.

We are committed to providing a sophisticated experience for all our patrons. To maintain this ambiance, we kindly request that all guests be 12 years of age or older. We appreciate your cooperation and understanding.

review.reviewBody:
We enjoyed an excellent meal, prepared with finess and excruiating detail. The extras were all appreciated and the presentation was superb. Wine service selections were excellent.  The oysters were stellar, my beets beautiful, and our shared Dover sole with simmered & roasted vegetables were  perfection. The dessert course was spectualar.
I did think the valet charge  at $20 was high, when the website stated less, but the retrieval was prompt even with lots of activity.

This is one of the finest dining experiences I've ever had.  I've eaten in Michelin starred restaurants all over the world: One, two, and three stars.  That is not a brag, I say it for reference.  This "One Star" restaurant is as good, and in some cases, better, than some of the three star restaurants I've been to.  I have no idea how this could not be ranked higher.  This is the first Michelin restaurant I've been to where there wasn't at least one course I didn't care for.  Every single course, including the beginning "Snax" (four of them), were inventive, beautifully presented, and absolutely scrumptious.  The chefs at this restaurant are geniuses.  But it's not just the chefs: Every member of the staff was kind, polite, fun, and at your attention at all times.  It's obvious they enjoy working there and that says a lot about the establishment.  I don't know if I can write to Michelin and ask them to re-evaluate Atlas but I'm going to try. By the way: The ambience was warm, calming, and very pleasing to enjoy.  Thank you Atlas for one of the finest experiences of my life.  And no: I"m  not the owner's brother!

Easily the best dining experience in Atlanta! The Chef's Tasting menu with wine pairings is one of the best meals that my wife and I have had the good fortune to savor. Atlas is absolutely beautiful inside, the music is surprising but works, the staff are amazingly attentive and respectful yet friendly, every bite that we had was exquisitely crafted while forming superbly beautiful pieces of art on our plates. The sommelier was masterful at explaining the wines that we were enjoying, and I have never had more perfectly paired wines.

Highly recommended for a truly special occasion!
Anthony was an incredible member of the team, who made our experience special. Celebrating 10 year anniversary.
An amazing experience.  Wonderful food, outstanding service.  Certainly deserving of its Michelin star.
Service and Ambience was beautiful from greet through check.  Food fell well short of expectations.
Amazing. The experience of a lifetime. I will always remember.

Chef Freddy and Team always give a next level experience.
The food, ambiance, service and entire experience were superb.
Can’t wait to return!

The chefs tasting menu and overall experience left us wanting more...

I suppose we can start with the service.

Reservation: 7:45. Me and guests all arrived by 8pm. Drinks were served along with "snax" and the first course. This came by 8:15.

Then from 8:15 till about 9:15, we are searching for our waitress to place more drink orders and to see where our next course is. Next course comes at 9:45 and from there on was consistent. We ended our meal at 11:45.

Now lets talk about the food, which was also a miss for us this time around.

The good stuff: Amazing avocado salad. The wasabi dressing was phenomenal. We paid for 2 extra supplements, of one which the Wagyu was also AMAZING. There was a berries dish (not what it sounds like) where the Pate was amazing. The drinks were also phenomenal.

Everything other course I would put in the mediocre / bad  category.

The bad stuff: Every other course was a hard miss. One of the supplements was an asparagus dish, and it was NOT good. There was absolutely no flavor, like they missed putting in salt? There was a few dishes that were swapped for our guest (due to dietary restrictions) that she sent back because as she described it "not my cup of tea". The waitress asked how the course was and we shared it wasn't good and she said she will talk to the chef but nothing came out of it. Even the bread basket had 3 kinds of bed, besides the pretzel roll, the other 2 were extremely dry and stale.

Overall the entire meal left something more to desire.

Atlas was absolutely fantastic!  My husband and I dined for the tasting menu and every course was designed elegantly and tasted incredible!

The service was also impeccable!  Well done Atlas team!

item.name: Quintessa Wine Dinner at Atlas
item.description:
We are pleased to invite you to a Quintessa Wine Dinner on April 29, 2026. Quintessa, a respected winery in Rutherford, Napa Valley, is celebrated for its biodynamic practices, diverse terroir, and signature Bordeaux-style red blend crafted from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, and Carmenere. Throughout the evening, we will also feature Illumination by Quintessa—a limited-production Sauvignon Blanc praised for its complexity, balance, and aging potential.

Enjoy an exclusive dining experience where culinary artistry meets exceptional wine. Bari Zelizer, Quintessa’s Regional Sales Director, will share insights into the winery’s philosophy, viticulture, and winemaking approach.

Chef Freddy Money has created a seasonal tasting menu in collaboration with Head Sommelier Mcswell Pereira. Their thoughtful pairings highlight the unique characteristics of Quintessa’s wines, creating a seamless and refined food and wine experience.

This intimate evening offers a unique opportunity to explore how place, cuisine, and storytelling come together.

item.name: Mother's Day Feast Celebration - Main Dining
item.description:
Celebrate Mother’s Day at Atlas in our main dining room with a chef-curated culinary experience honoring all mothers and the moments that bring us together. Featuring a grand selection of seasonal dishes, each offering is thoughtfully crafted as an elevated interpretation of beloved favorites, inviting guests to explore a refined and abundant culinary experience at their own pace.

Offered exclusively for the occasion, this experience blends the warmth of tradition with Atlas’ signature culinary artistry, an elegant expression of appreciation for the women we celebrate.

Please note that our regular à la carte menu will not be available during this experience.

We look forward to welcoming you and yours for a memorable Mother’s Day at Atlas.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Atlas is an excellent choice for date night. Guests consistently praise the intimate, art-filled dining room, refined multi-course tasting menu and attentive service that make special occasions feel memorable. Expect fine‑dining pacing, theatrical desserts (the rose dessert is a highlight) and a well-curated wine program. It’s on the pricey side, so plan for a longer, celebratory evening and consider early seating if you prefer a quieter table.

mainEntity.name: What are the portion sizes like at this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portions at Atlas are small and tasting‑menu focused, expect many artfully plated courses rather than large entrées. Guests often describe the chef’s tasting as several small, highly composed courses; à la carte portions are still refined. If you want extra substance, many guests add supplements (like Westholme Wagyu or Dover sole for two) or the cheese cart. Plan for a leisurely multi‑course experience rather than a single large plate.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant serve alcohol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Atlas has a comprehensive beverage program. Guests rave about expertly crafted cocktails, an extensive wine list and thoughtful wine pairings for the tasting menu. Luxury offerings (Dom Pérignon cocktails, Louis XIII cognac) and upscale cocktails are offered alongside non‑alcoholic flights. The sommelier team is frequently praised for knowledgeable recommendations.

mainEntity.name: What is this restaurant's stand-out or favorite dish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Atlas is best known for its Chef’s Tasting Menu highlights, standouts mentioned repeatedly include the FM Rocher dessert, Dover sole for two, standout seafood dishes (halibut/turbot) and the Westholme Wagyu supplement. Guests also single out the cheese cart and the theatrical La Vie En Rose dessert. If you’re unsure, many guests recommend the tasting menu with a wine pairing or adding the wagyu supplement.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have accessible or family-friendly seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partially, Atlas regularly welcomes families and celebratory groups; guests report bringing teens and celebrating birthdays and anniversaries. The dining room feels intimate with a mix of booths, two‑tops and four‑tops. If you need accessible seating or a quieter table for family dining, call ahead so staff can assist, guests note staff are accommodating about substitutions and special requests.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Atlas?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a quieter experience, aim for an early weekday dinner (Tuesday–Thursday) or an early seating when service tends to be calmer. Weekends, holidays and special dates (Valentine’s Day, Saturdays) are busier and can be louder; several guests reported longer waits, louder music or bar seating on peak nights. Reservations are recommended, and arriving a little early to enjoy the bar is popular.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Atlas balances elegant, art‑filled fine dining with playful culinary surprises. The dining room is moody and refined, emerald green walls showcase major 20th‑century art, while the service team is highly attentive. Guests frequently praise the theatrical, polished service and creative plating, though some note louder or stylistically mismatched music on busy nights. Overall it reads as upscale, warm and memorable.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Atlas?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dress code is smart casual. Guests commonly dress up for special occasions, many reviews note jackets and elegant attire, but Atlas is not strictly formal. If you’re celebrating, a polished smart‑casual outfit fits the room and atmosphere.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have vegan/vegetarian, gluten-free or other dietary options?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Atlas offers vegetarian and vegan tasting menus and can accommodate dietary needs when contacted in advance. Guests report successful vegetarian and vegan tasting experiences and staff accommodating allergies (including celiac disease) with gluten‑free options and separate gluten‑free bread. Always mention restrictions when booking so the kitchen can prepare substitutions.

mainEntity.name: Can I make any special requests before I arrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, guests frequently report that staff accommodate special requests like dietary substitutions, anniversary acknowledgements and seating preferences. Mention requests when you make your reservation (or call ahead), Atlas has a history of providing celebratory touches (cards, complimentary desserts) and modifying dishes for allergies or preferences.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant kid-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Families do dine at Atlas and guests sometimes bring teens or celebrate birthdays with children. The focus is on an elevated tasting experience, so there isn’t a children’s menu, portions are small and pacing is leisurely. For younger children consider early seating, the tavern/bar area for a more casual vibe, or call ahead to discuss menu flexibility.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Atlas is busiest on weekend nights, holidays and special occasions (Valentine’s Day, NYE) when guests report louder rooms and full dining schedules. Quietest times tend to be early weeknights (Tuesday–Thursday) and early dinner seatings, perfect if you prefer a calmer pace. Regardless, reserve ahead; tasting menus are paced and often fill evening slots.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to Atlas?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a more relaxed experience, choose a weekday (Tuesday–Thursday). Guests report that weekend nights and holidays are lively and can be louder or more crowded. If you want the full tasting menu without the busiest room, an early weekday dinner is often the best balance of service and atmosphere.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant open on public holidays?

acceptedAnswer.text: Specific holiday hours are not provided in the public information. Guests have dined at Atlas on holidays (Christmas Eve, Thanksgiving, New Year’s Eve) and report special holiday menus and busy service; call the restaurant or check their site for holiday hours and special event offerings before booking.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any special awards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Atlas is a Michelin One‑Star restaurant (2023). Guests and critics consistently reference the Michelin honor as well as high praise for the culinary team, service and wine program.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any specials deals or experiences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Atlas offers curated experiences rather than everyday discounts, notable options include the Chef’s multi‑course tasting menu, vegetarian/vegan tasting menus, wine pairing flights and occasional special four‑hands or collaboration dinners. Guests also highlight the cheese cart, theatrical desserts (La Vie En Rose) and optional supplements like wagyu and Dover sole for two as elevated add‑ons.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have dynamic or rotating menus?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Atlas runs seasonal and rotating tasting menus. Guests frequently reference the changing Chef’s Tasting Menu, seasonal ingredients (white asparagus, seasonal seafood) and collaborations that alter the menu. The restaurant emphasizes ingredient provenance and creativity, so expect menu updates.

mainEntity.name: How is Atlas restaurant rated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Atlas is rated 4.9 stars by 2364 OpenTable diners.

mainEntity.name: Does Atlas offer gift cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Atlas does offer gift cards which you can purchase here.

mainEntity.name: Is Atlas currently accepting reservations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can generally book this restaurant by choosing the date, time and party size on OpenTable.

content.body: Atlanta’s crown jewel of fine dining, Bacchanalia is a perfect special occasion restaurant — ever-reliable and seasonal in nature, meaning it’s different every time.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Bacchanalia has well-earned its reputation as Atlanta's most-celebrated restaurant since opening in 1993. Touted as the "monarch" of "fine-dining terrain" by Atlanta Magazine, chef-owner Anne Quatrano and Clifford Harrison's elegant establishment features contemporary American cuisine executed by a crack culinary team lead by chef Kai Na'Lampoon. The kitchen produces a seasonal and ever-changing four course menu each night that relies entirely on organic ingredients (many sourced from Anne and Clifford's farm, Summerland), providing a fresh experience for each unique visit.

tagline.body: Because it refuses to ever grow staid, this restaurant always can and will surprise you. —AJC

why_we_like_it.body: Atlanta’s crown jewel of fine dining, Bacchanalia is a perfect special occasion restaurant — ever-reliable and seasonal in nature, meaning it’s different every time.

en-us: Bacchanalia offers a four course, prix fixe menu at $140. per person.
The menu evolves slightly each evening and throughout the seasons.
We offer a wine pairing suggestions with many of the menu options.

content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Hayakawa is an intimate and traditional sushiya in the mold of the finest sushi shops in Japan. Newly located in West Midtown Atlanta, our serenely designed space allows for guests to have a truly unique experience. Chef Atsushi Hayakawa curates the finest fish selection in Atlanta, sourcing from Tokyo's Toyosu market and all over the globe. A staple of Atlanta since 2008, we invite you to join us for an experience rarely found outside of Japan.

need_to_know.body:
Please look over all of the following before dining with us: 
our policies, parking information, and contact information. Customers with allergies or dietary restrictions who are not acquainted with our cuisine are still bound by our cancellation policy. We politely ask guests not to wear perfume or cologne to ensure it does not disrupt the dining experience for others.
All can be found via the links below.
We provide a reservation only 16-course Omakase Dinner at 6:00pm and 8:30pm, Wednesday through Saturday.
Our booking window operates on a 30-day rolling period meaning that instead of being limited to booking reservations one month in advance, you are able to book up to 30 days ahead from the current date. Reservations are live at 12pm.

Hope to see you soon!

ld_json.name: Mujō
ld_json.description: Mujō is a one MICHELIN star, intimate, omakase-only tasting menu experience serving modern edomae sushi led by Executive Chef J. Trent Harris.  Our menu changes daily and reflects the best seasonal ingredients available, as well as fish flown in directly from Japan.  The experience consists of a series of small plates and a progression of seasonal nigiri.  We are inspired by the Japanese concept of ichi-go ichi-e, 一期一会, or “one time, one meeting.  Our goal is not to recreate the sushiya of Japan, but to offer an experience that represents who and where we are, while respecting and honoring the traditions of edomae sushi. Inspired by the concept of omotenashi, but rooted in southern hospitality.
ld_json.openingHours: Wed–Sat 5:30 pm–11:30 pm

review.reviewBody: Excellent food and service- a gem! First time there and will definitely be back

￼We had a spectacular dining experience while celebrating my birthday. From the moment we walked through the door, we were greeted like family and treated with so much care and grace. The food was spectacular and the chef was engaging with over two decades of experience.  He shared so much knowledge and his passion for his craft was infectious. The food was delicious beautifully displayed, and every course was better than the next. We added on the Wagyu beef, a carrot dish and the caviar.  We were so stuffed but enjoyed every morsel. There is a reason why this restaurant has been recognized by Michelin three times and was the absolute best meal and service we’ve ever had in Atlanta.  We will be back and recommend it if you wanted exceptional dining experience.

High end (expensive) sushi experiences have become popular , especially in Atlanta. I am still trying to decide if this value is truly about the food and experience or the price tag and the difficulty in getting reservations. 
Specific to this experience ….in the context of a 2k experience for four people in an exclusive room (Koshitsu counter), incredibly friendly service, very engaged. Did not miss an opportunity to enhance . 
The food, I would have to say was average. A couple of the presentations were memorable but most were just good. The nigiri fish was well cut but the rice was not constructed to hold well. I felt the wasabi was overdone and really hid the flavors. The portions were small even for nigiri and the communication about the presentations was  limited to just a few words ( it’s supposed to be an experience). . As the conversation continued, the wonderfully friendly chef shared that he actually grew up in the South and had worked his way up to sushi chef over the four years in employment at Mujō. This critique is not about him but  in the context of an expensive night….. we would have appreciated more consideration of the situation perhaps a senior chef or perhaps have been honored by Chef Hayashi. Have heard so much about Mujō . Just expected a “wow”. Sad to say that we cannot recommend it.
Great food staff made the night special. They were attentive professional. Most of all they made it personable.

My wife and I went to Mujō last night. Words can’t describe how incredible the experience was. From the cocktails before we were seated to the last bite every second was perfectly crafted to provide an experience that I will never forget. Every person we interacted with was incredible and every bite of food was an eye opening realization of what sushi could be.

This was by far the best experience and meal I’ve ever had. From the curated menu, service, hospitality, explanation of the meal, beverage pairings, and level of respect - everything was absolutely outstanding. It is definitely an investment, but well worth it for a lovely and highly memorable time.
Amazing experience!  Food and service were amazing.
Nice experience, just wildly overpriced. Have had plenty of similar quality omakase for half the price of this or less.

This was a once in a lifetime experience that I didn’t want to end. It was intimate, sexy, and service was 100/10. Food was unique, delicious, and every bite was better than the last if that’s possible. I will be dreaming of this forever.

item.name: Sushi Counter - Seasonal Omakase
item.description:
Mujō is an omakase-only, tasting menu experience. Our menu changes daily and reflects the best seasonal ingredients available, as well as fish flown in directly from Japan. A supplemental menu of specialty items and optional beverage pairings are available for an additional charge. 

The price of our seasonal omakase menu is $245 per person.  Our corkage fee is $100 per 750mL bottle, with a 2 bottle limit.  Please make sure to consult with the restaurant (call/email) prior to bringing bottles, as any wine/sake that is on the list can not be accepted as corkage. 

A credit card is required to hold this reservation.  The credit card will only be charged in the event of violation of our cancellation policy.

item.description:
The Koshitsu Counter can accommodate four to six guests and is seated once per evening at 7pm.  Guests can expect to enjoy our season omakase menu which includes a series of small plates followed by a progression of seasonal nigiri and dessert. The price per person for this experience starts at $275.  A supplemental menu of specialty items will be offered for additional charge. A team member will contact you directly to arrange the deposit and answer any questions. The deposit is non-refundable within 2 weeks of the booking.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Mujō is an intimate, Michelin-starred omakase that many guests recommend for dates and special occasions. The dim, focused lighting, counter seating and attentive service create a romantic, Tokyo-like atmosphere ideal for anniversaries or a memorable night out. Consider arriving a bit early to enjoy cocktails at the bar and plan for a multi-course tasting that lasts 1.5–2.5 hours. It’s a splurge, but guests frequently say it’s worth it for celebrations.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Mujō?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best time is for an evening reservation during Wed–Sat service, arrive a little early if you’d like a pre-dinner cocktail at the bar. For slightly quieter service and easier availability, aim for earlier seatings midweek (Wednesday or Thursday) or the first seating of the night. If you want a lively special-occasion vibe, weekend seatings are popular but busier.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ambience is refined, intimate and theatrical, focused lighting, a dark room, and close chef interaction create a Tokyo-like omakase vibe. Service is consistently described as warm, attentive and highly professional. Note that some guests find the music choices and volume eclectic or loud at times, so it’s lively rather than hushed fine dining.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Mujō?

acceptedAnswer.text: Business casual is the recommended dress code. Many guests treat Mujō as a special-occasion spot, so smart, polished attire fits the elegant omakase setting.

mainEntity.name: Can I make any special requests before I arrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the team is used to accommodating dietary restrictions, celebrations and special requests. Guests report that staff have made allergy accommodations and added celebratory touches; to ensure the best experience, call or note requests when you book so the chefs and front‑of‑house can prepare.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant kid-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Families do dine at Mujō for special occasions, and guests often bring teens or celebrate birthdays with children. The focus is on a formal omakase tasting, there’s no kids’ menu, and the space is compact, so younger children or strollers may be challenging. If visiting with kids, consider an earlier seating or a private-party option and call ahead to discuss flexibility.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Busiest: weekend evening seatings (weekends are popular for celebrations). Quietest: earlier seatings and midweek nights tend to be calmer, although Mujō only operates Wed–Sat, so Wednesday/Thursday earlier seatings are usually the least crowded. If you prefer a quieter pace, request an earlier reservation or first seating.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to Mujō?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wednesday or Thursday evenings are often the best bet for slightly easier availability and a quieter experience, while still enjoying full service. If you’re celebrating or want a livelier atmosphere, weekend nights are very popular but also busier, book early either way, as seating is limited.

content.body: The Easton Porter Group is no stranger to inventive haute cuisine (as fine-dining star The Restaurant at Zero George proves) and Wild Common is no different. Here, James Beard-nominated chef Orlando Pagán makes magic as he dips into international influences and a local pantry for his tasting menus. Oh, and do get the optional wine pairings — they tend to begin with Champagne.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body:
Executive Chef Orlando Pagán delivers a multi-course tasting of wildly uncommon cuisine, showcasing the best local, seasonal ingredients. Guests are invited to enjoy dinner service in the restaurant’s indoor dining room, the private courtyard, or at the Chef’s Counter to watch Chef Orlando Pagán and team up close in action.  

For information about our semi-private dining room, The Overlook, or for reservations for parties of 7 or more, please call us at 843.817.7311 or send an email to info@wildcommoncharleston.com.

need_to_know.body:
We serve a Chef’s Tasting Menu Wednesday–Sunday, with reservations opening 30 days in advance. Executive Chef Orlando Pagán presents a multi-course tasting of wildly uncommon cuisine, showcasing the best local and seasonal ingredients. Guests are invited to dine in our indoor dining room, surrounded by curated Lowcountry art in partnership with the Charleston Artist Collective.

Our experience is chef-driven and seasonally inspired, highlighting creativity, balance, and a sense of place. Rather than ordering from a traditional à la carte menu, guests embark on a guided culinary journey designed by Chef Pagán and the Wild Common team.

The menu is pre-set and changes frequently. To ensure you experience the menu as Chef Pagán originally envisioned, we make as few substitutions as possible.

Accommodations: We are happy to accommodate certain dietary restrictions with advance notice—vegetarian, pescatarian, shellfish allergy, and nut allergy. However, we are unable to accommodate gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free, fin-fish allergy, or vegan menus.

Allergens: While we take care in preparation, we cannot guarantee that food is prepared in an allergen-free environment due to the size of our kitchens and the complexity of our menus. Please call us 72 hours before your reservation with any allergies or dietary concerns.

Timing: Plan to arrive 5–10 minutes before your reservation to enjoy the full experience; the tasting menu is paced intentionally over several courses, and dinner will last around an hour and a half. 

Groups: For parties of 7 or more, please contact us at 843-817-7311 or info@wildcommoncharleston.com.

Parking: Available on surrounding streets and at 216 Rutledge Ave in the "Cannon Green Event Parking" lot.

Seating: Courtyard seating is subject to weather and private events. When unavailable, we will honor your reservation in our dining room.

tagline.body: Anything but common fare, wildly welcoming hospitality.

why_we_like_it.body: The Easton Porter Group is no stranger to inventive haute cuisine (as fine-dining star The Restaurant at Zero George proves) and Wild Common is no different. ld_json.name: la Barbecue
ld_json.description: Chef Ali Clem is the owner and pitmaster behind la Barbecue, the Michelin-starred Austin destination renowned for its Texas-style smoked brisket. Trained under barbecue legend John Mueller, Ali—alongside her late wife and co-founder LeAnn Mueller—turned a humble South First Street trailer into one of the most celebrated barbecue joints in the world. Consistently ranked among the best by Texas Monthly and now honored with a Michelin Star, la Barbecue is known for its expertly smoked meats, bold flavors, and uncompromising quality. Located just minutes from downtown Austin and iconic South Congress, the restaurant offers a lively yet welcoming atmosphere, complete with a laid-back patio space that invites guests to relax, gather, and enjoy true Central Texas barbecue at its finest.
ld_json.openingHours: Wed–Sun 11:00 am–6:00 pm

review.reviewBody: The best barbecue I've ever had. Well deserving of their Michelin Star!

Absolutely incredible barbecue. Every component from the brisket and pork ribs to the slaw and kimchi had a depth of flavor that was second to none. The sauces had a little bit of a spicy kick but also a bit of sweetness that you could tell was crafted by experts who love what they do! 10/10.

Great tasting food but once the hostess found out I had a reservation (that THEY allow and I made weeks ahead) she was not happy to a point that I felt a little out-of-place. This curbed my excitement and we left as soon as we could 🤷‍♂️

Maybe I’m wrong to make a reservation and should’ve waited in line? idk

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, la Barbecue can make a memorable date-night spot if you and your guest enjoy high-quality Texas-style smoked meats in a relaxed setting. The Michelin recognition and rave guest comments about the brisket and ribs make it a special culinary experience, while the laid-back patio and casual dress code keep things comfortable rather than formal. Note one guest felt awkward about a reservation interaction, so consider calling ahead or planning an early seating to ensure a smooth arrival.

mainEntity.name: What are this restaurant's opening hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: la Barbecue is open Wednesday through Sunday from 11:00 am to 6:00 pm. Those are the published hours from the restaurant, so plan your visit within that window and consider arriving earlier in the day for the best selection of smoked meats.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The atmosphere is lively yet welcoming, Michelin-starred barbecue served in a casual, unfussy setting. Guests praise deeply flavored smoked meats, and the patio adds a relaxed, social vibe ideal for groups or a casual date. Expect energetic, down-to-earth service and a focus on expertly prepared Central Texas barbecue rather than formal fine-dining frills.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for la Barbecue?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casual dress is appropriate at la Barbecue. The restaurant balances Michelin-star quality with a relaxed, casual-dining environment, so comfortable, neat attire is perfectly suitable, think casual weekend clothes rather than formal wear.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to la Barbecue?

acceptedAnswer.text: la Barbecue is open Wednesday through Sunday, so any of those days will work. If you prefer a quieter experience, try a midweek visit (Wednesday or Thursday) soon after opening at 11:00 am, that timing can help you avoid peak weekend crowds and get the best selection of smoked meats.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have outdoor seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, la Barbecue features a laid-back patio space where guests can relax and enjoy their barbecue outdoors. The patio contributes to the casual, social vibe and is a good option if you prefer outdoor seating.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any special awards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, la Barbecue is a Michelin 1 Star (2025) recipient and has been consistently ranked among the best by Texas Monthly. Those honors reflect the restaurant’s reputation for expertly smoked meats and bold, carefully developed flavors.

ld_json.name: Restaurant Mixtli
ld_json.description:
MIXTLI

MEESH-LEE, MIX-TLI / has the variant form MEX-TLI: Aztec spoken word for cloud.

THE CLOUD

To define Mexican cuisine is impossible. Mexico is as diverse as it is vast. Within its borders lie rocky mountains, humid jungles, arid deserts, and endless coasts: a stark diversity that forced each region to develop uniquely rich cultural and culinary histories.

Like clouds, our menu travels from place to place offering a tour in Mexican gastronomy. If the state has a border with the ocean, we start our trek on the coast and work inland, bringing dishes specifically from that region or state. After each season, the cloud travels to other lands and we begin again.

It is our mission that you fall in love with Mexico.

content_body_translations.translation:
都会の喧騒から少し離れた赤坂２丁目に位置するフレンチレストラン。
世界的デザイナー森田恭通氏によるヴェルサイユ宮殿の可憐さを、現代のフィルターを通して表現された輝かしい空間で、優雅なひとときを。
2022~2024年にかけて3年連続ミシュラン一つ星を獲得し、多くのゲストを魅了してきた鳴海陽人シェフによる日本のエッセンスを散りばめた四季折々の料理。
お料理を引き立てるフランス産をベースに世界各国から厳選された銘醸ワインとともに心行くまでお楽しみください。

Authentic cuisine prepared by a French-trained chef
由法國培訓的廚師準備的正宗美食

content_body_translations.translation: シンプルで優しい光のおしゃれな雰囲気の空間で独創的なフレンチをご堪能いただけます。厳選された素材本来の味を引き出すため、バターや生クリームをほとんど使わずに仕上げた軽やかでヘルシーなメニューをお楽しみください。味わいだけでなくプレゼンテーションにもこだわり、見た目にも美しい料理の数々。シェフの自由な発想のもと生まれた料理はどれも新しく、他のレストランではなかなか召し上がることのできないものばかりです。

Enjoy creative French dishes in a relaxed and simple and also stylish setting. We serve a light and healthy which uses only a limited amount of butter and fresh cream to ensure you enjoy the original taste of our carefully selected ingredients. Our dishes are beautifully presented as well as delicious, innovatively crafted and created by our chefs. You will not find food like this anywhere else.
在一個用吉野雪松制作的櫃檯上, 在精緻的氣氛中，享受一頓美餐。我們的廚師用優質的食材準備美味的菜肴, 並用美味的蔬菜进行摆盘,创意来自于由紀夫農民或長野 Tonomi。我們所有的食物都制作成日本式的风味, 如Aritayaki瓷, 為您帶來東西方的最佳搭配。

ld_json.name: PRIMO PASSO
ld_json.description:
PRIMO PASSOは、"美食としてのパスタ"を追求するイタリア料理店です。

シェフは、南イタリア・ナポリ近郊の三つ星店でパスタ部門の責任者を務めた藤岡 智之。
移ろう四季の恵みを感じる食材と和の技法を取り入れた、
全12品の「おまかせ」コースには、シェフの"パスタの奥深さを体験してほしい"という
想いから、5品の多彩なパスタを組み込みました。

和のしつらえを基調とした空間で、ゆったりと食事の時間をお楽しみください。
皆様のご来店を心よりお待ち申し上げております。

ld_json.name: 帝国ホテル 寅黒
ld_json.description:
帝国ホテル 寅黒は、
現代の日本料理を代表するミシュラン3つ星の名店、「神楽坂 石かわ」「虎白」と帝国ホテルとの
提携が実現した店舗です。
世紀を超えてフランス料理を築いてきた帝国ホテルが、新たな和食文化をお届けします。

お食事は旬の食材の持つ旨みを引き出し、
カウンターで展開される炭焼き・蒸し物の臨場感を大事にした
高級日本料理のおまかせコースをご提供いたします。

ld_json.name: Kappo Sato
ld_json.description:
Kappo Sato is the newest Kappo-style Japanese Cuisine in Toronto, Canada featuring Takeshi Sato. 

Takeshi Sato worked at a Michelin Star Japanese restaurant in Tokyo and came to Canada in 2011 as the official chef of the Japanese Consulate General in Toronto. Qualified as a tea ceremony, flower arrangement, sommelier, and international sake master, and has more than 20 years of experience as a high-class Japanese chef, as well as the skill and knowledge.

result.name: Reserve a table at Kappo Sato

ld_json.name: Kaiseki Yu-zen Hashimoto Restaurant
ld_json.description:
Owner and Chef Masaki Hashimoto offers a traditional Kaiseki experience outside of Japan. Nestled in the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre in North York, this restaurant will transport you to Kyoto for an evening. It is a beautiful sensory journey of textures, flavors, and aromas, all captured in a quiet and peaceful environment. Away from the hustle and bustle of a busy restaurant scene. 

Serving only 3 tables a night, one seating per table, relax and have a glass of saké. Every day is an occasion. Life is worth celebrating with an authentic Kaiseki meal.

result.name: Reserve a table at Kaiseki Yu-zen Hashimoto Restaurant

ld_json.name: aKin
ld_json.description:
We are currently taking reservations for all days up to and including May 31st.

aKin is a modern Asian fine dining restaurant offering a 10-course blind tasting menu that showcases innovative spins on classic dishes using local and seasonal ingredients.

The intimate space, designed with custom elements and a focus on detail, provides a personalized experience with seating for 28 guests in the main dining room, 4 at the chef’s counter, and an 8-person private dining room. 

With a commitment to excellence, aKin blends tradition and creativity, aiming to push culinary boundaries and offer a unique dining journey.

ld_json.name: The Pine
ld_json.description: Located in a converted former gas station in the heart of the charming village of Creemore, The Pine offers an intimate and immersive tasting menu experience. Chef Jeremy Austin crafts an ever-evolving journey that draws on Canada’s diverse landscapes to tell evocative stories inspired by flavours from far beyond our borders.

result.name: Reserve a table at The Pine

ld_json.name: Sushi Masaki Saito
ld_json.description:
Sushi Masaki Saito is a high-end, traditional sushi omakase restaurant. It is the first and  restaurant in Canada with a two Michelin-starred chef. Chef Masaki Saito, raised in Hokkaido and trained in Tokyo, focuses on the purity and source of his ingredients, and showcases his respect for Edomae tradition in evolution with his own unique imagination.
Tucked into a cozy Victorian building in Yorkville, Sushi Masaki Saito reveals the tradition and atmosphere of Gion, Kyoto or an Old Edo-style neighbourhood in Tokyo. Every detail serves the aim of authenticity, including a 200-year old Hinoki dining counter imported from Nara, Japan that is surrounded by a harmony of traditional Japanese handcrafted décor and local Ontario marble and limestone.

result.name: Reserve a table at Sushi Masaki Saito

ld_json.name: Shoushin
ld_json.description:
At Shoushin, guests are greeted by a 200 year old Hinoki wood counter where true sushi craftsmanship unfolds.   Offering a traditional Omakase experience, Michelin starred Chef Jackie Lin goes to great lengths to procure the best. 

Using exclusively wild caught fish, the menu features seasonal fish sourced from Toyosu fish Market for a truly elevated dining experience.  With a commitment to bringing our diners the finest Edomae style sushi outside of Japan,  the minimalist Japanese aesthetic, the quality of our ingredients as well as our exquisite omontenashi – Japanese hospitality, are the core tenets to your next omakase experience.

ld_json.name: Edulis Restaurant
ld_json.description:
Bookings now open through to the end of April.
May bookings will open on April 15th at 6 pm. Please note we will be closed for a Spring Holiday from May 3 to 17th.

A reminder as always that our restaurant is extremely small and we have very few tables - if you don't see the reservation you desire, please make use of the "notify" waitlist function and we will be in touch if we are able to accommodate your request!

Please scroll down to see our FAQ section for more information about our pre-paid menu policies and about booking with any dietary restrictions. 

Edulis is about many things – the pleasure of enjoying a gathering around the table to share dishes and to be greeted like a friend; conviviality, feasting, celebrating the craft and tradition of cooking and spectacular ingredients. As the season unfolds, so does our inspiration. Our menus change to showcase the ingredients of the moment.

result.name: Reserve a table at Edulis Restaurant

ld_json.name: Restaurant 20 Victoria
ld_json.description:
We’re pleased to welcome you to book reservations for the month MAY. JUNE reservations will be released online Monday May 11th at 11:00am. 

Our Dining Room offers  a 7+ course set menu, and our Kitchen Gallery offers a 4-course set menu from Wednesday through Friday. On Saturdays, the Kitchen Gallery features the 7+ course tasting menu.
Our menus change at whim, guided by the finest meticulously sourced products from Ontario and our coastal regions, enriched by our team’s diverse heritage. 
In addition to a thoughtfully curated wine list, we offer an optional beverage pairing to accompany your meal.

20 Victoria is an intimate space with a limited number of tables. We host parties of 2 and 4 in our Dining Room, and parties of 2 in our Kitchen Gallery. If you don’t see availability for your preferred date and time, please join our waitlist—we will always do our best to accommodate you.

result.name: Reserve a table at Restaurant 20 Victoria

ld_json.name: Beckon
ld_json.description: Dining at Beckon is a notable event that remarks on the changing aesthetic of the Colorado seasons.  Our menu is shaped by ingredients served at their peak and in congruence with the culinary calendar. These dishes reflect the natural rhythm of the year, offering a dynamic and ever-changing dining experience in tune with the world around us. We are committed to our relationships with ambitious purveyors and remarkable producers of fine, quality ingredients, and loyally support those that go above and beyond to provide an exemplary product for the table.

ld_json.name: Margot
ld_json.description: Inspired by the bonne vivante who always finds themselves at the right place at the right time, join Margot for an unassuming tasting experience. With thoughtful flavor combinations from Sicily, Japan, the Americas, and of course France, Margot represents contemporary American cuisine. Expect innovative, seasonally-driven dishes that will elevate your evening.

ld_json.name: Frasca Food and Wine
ld_json.description: Frasca Food and Wine is the James Beard Foundation Award winning-concept from Partners Bobby Stuckey, Lachlan Mackinnon-Patterson and Peter Hoglund. Steeped in food and wine traditions of the northeastern region of Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Frasca Food and Wine welcomes guests in nightly with warm hospitality, exceptional cuisine and expertly selected wines.

result.name: Reserve a table at Frasca Food and Wine

Our goal is to create a restorative and memorable experience for every guest. Whether it’s the artistry of each dish or the personal connection shared over the counter, we aim to bring warmth and authenticity to every moment.

We look forward to welcoming you to a culinary journey rooted in seasonality, creativity, and heartfelt hospitality.

about.body: Nari is a modern Thai restaurant, merging traditional techniques with the seasonal bounty of California. Served family style, our heritage driven cuisine is enhanced with exceptional service, amazing cocktails and an extensive wine list.

need_to_know.body:
STRICT CANCELLATIONS: We require 24 hours notice for cancellations to avoid a $20 per person fee (parties of 1-5). Same day bookings + cancellations are considered no shows.

DIETARY RESTRICTIONS: Nari cannot accommodate severe celiac, peanut, or shellfish allergies, sugar or allium restrictions, or guests who are simultaneously vegetarian and gluten free. Please email info@narisf.com to discuss ALL restrictions as we may not be able to accommodate without advanced notice. 

LOUNGE + MEZZANINE DINING: Nari serves the full a la carte menu in the mezzanine bar, while the Chef's Pick is only available in the main dining room and for lounge reservations.

NARI ENTRANCE: The entrance to Nari is located through the lobby of Hotel Kabuki, which is also accessible by the Japantown Center Garage.

PARKING: Please allow ample time to find parking on the street or in the Japantown Center Garage as we are only able to hold the table for 15 minutes. We may not be able to accommodate if you arrive later than 15 minutes.

We encourage you to visit the FAQ page on narisf.com for more information on our policies.

about.body: Michelin-starred Kin Khao serves delicious Thai food that stays true to its origin, marrying California seasonal produce and sustainably raised or caught meats and seafood with daily house-made curry pastes, sauces, and relishes. Imbibe in fun and inventive cocktails like a gin-based "Tom Yum" and a wine list featuring world-renowned Rieslings. Take a peek at the Lunch and Dinner offerings on the website www.kinkhao.com as these menus are different!
