ld_json.description:
UKA will be relocating from Japan House Los Angeles at the end of 2025 as we prepare for an exciting new chapter. Since opening in 2023, we’ve been honored to share authentic Japanese kaiseki and are grateful for the support that helped us earn Michelin stars in both 2024 and 2025. Our last day of service at the current location will be December 31, 2025. We look forward to expanding our vision and elevating the dining experience at our new home, which will be announced soon. Thank you for your continued support—we can’t wait to welcome you to our next location.

December - a season of celebration, connection, and unforgettable moments.

This holiday season, UKA invites you to indulge in our Special Holiday Kaiseki Experience — a refined multi-course journey crafted with the finest seasonal ingredients.

Holiday Kaiseki Experience - 12/3/2025 - 12/31/2025
- 6:30 PM seatings (Chef's Counter & Table Seating)
- $450 per guest*
- Includes a welcome drink - a special holiday gift from us

Celebrate this festive time with us at UKA. We look forward to welcoming you and making your holiday truly memorable.

*Tax, gratuity, and additional beverages are not included.

Dining Experience Options
We currently offer two unique dining experiences, each with its own seating time:

1. Signature Course – "Kaiseki Experience" Seating Time: 6:30 PM (Only)
* Chef’s Counter: Enjoy an intimate, front-row seat to Chef Mitsue’s culinary artistry, with direct interaction as each course is prepared.
* Table Seating: A more private option that still offers a view of the kitchen and the chef in action.

2. Flexible Dining Course – Chef’s Recommended Assortments & Dishes Starting Time: 8:30 PM (Only) This course offers a more casual introduction to our Michelin-starred cuisine without the full Kaiseki commitment.
* Prefixed Menu: Choose from a curated 3-course ($75) or 5-course ($150) menu featuring seasonal selections.
* À la Carte Menu: Select from individual dishes crafted with the same premium ingredients, designed to pair beautifully with our sake and beverage offerings.



Located in JAPAN HOUSE Los Angeles perched high above Hollywood Blvd., UKA introduces the Kaiseki haute culinary tradition of a multi-course, intricate Japanese dinner to a modern-day palate with a refined omakase menu that seeks to capture a particular essence of time and place.

UKA, a Michelin One-Star restaurant listed in the Michelin Guide California 2024 & 2025. 

Reservation structure, UKA will only be accepting reservations at 6:30 PM. Guests can choose to be seated at the Chef's Counter, where they can engage directly with Chef Mitsue, or at our table seating for a more private setting, while still enjoying a view of the counter where Chef Mitsue prepares the dishes.

Chef's recommended assortments & dishes, starting at 8:30 PM. While we highly recommend making reservations, we warmly welcome guests who wish to experience our Michelin One-Star dining without committing to the full course. This new offering gives you a choice to start with a prefixed assortment to start your evening with a taste of Kaiseki or order appetizers for small bites, using the same high-quality ingredients from our course meals but arranged differently to pair perfectly with the drinks we offer.

We invite guests to join us and enjoy the stunning view of Hollywood, complemented by the exclusive UKA dining ambiance.

*Menus and prices are subject to change without notice. Ingredients and course details may vary daily.
*Special Requests: Please include any special requests in the notes section during reservation checkout or contact us in advance.
*Children & Service Dogs: We kindly ask that you mention in the special requests if you will be attending with a Child (under 13 years old) or a service dog.
*Dietary Restrictions: While we strive to accommodate all dietary restrictions and allergies, please understand that due to our ingredients and food preparation methods, certain accommodations may be challenging. Kindly note any restrictions in the special requests section or email us in advance.

about.body: Michelin-starred modern French bistro, Camphor, is located in Downtown LA’s Arts District and is a testament to the visionary approach of No. 8 Hospitality, a premier hospitality and development group. Owned and operated by Sarah Lam and Cyrus Batchan, No. 8 has cultivated Camphor into a dining destination that re-imagines the classic bistro experience. Under the culinary direction of Executive Chef Max Boonthanakit, Camphor offers a unique flavor identity through an unassuming yet nuanced menu, drawing from Chef Max Boonthanakit’s global upbringing and classical French training. No. 8’s commitment to excellence is evident in every aspect of Camphor, from its intentionally designed convivial atmosphere and welcoming hospitality to its unpretentious and enticing menu. Guests can indulge in shareable small plates, heartier mains, scenographic desserts, classic cocktails with a French twist, and an enviable selection of French and European wines, all curated to reflect the distinctive culinary vision that No. 8 brings to the table.

ld_json.name: Cyrus
ld_json.description:
Unique in California Wine Country, this pastoral restaurant floats above the vines with panoramic views of Alexander Valley. Chef Douglas Keane’s distinctive Dining Journey is a progressive tasting menu designed to transport each guest through a series of spaces and experiences.
An evening at Cyrus begins in the Bubbles Lounge where a glittering Champagne and Martini cart beckons. A welcoming treat appears from the kitchen as guests sip libations, free to sink into a leather lounge chair or wander the gardens and take in the vineyard views. The journey then moves to the Kitchen Table where diners engage with the chefs and observe as courses are prepared before them with the spectacle of the bustling kitchen beyond.
The next leg of the journey brings each party to their table in the dining room with its sweeping views of Alexander Valley. A succession of beautifully plated courses finishing with dessert and sweet bites follows. The last stop of the evening’s tour leads to the mysterious Chocolate Room with a final surprise and a parting gift of house-made chocolate.

SF Chronicle Review: https://www.sfchronicle.com/food/restaurants/article/cyrus-fine-dining-17572226.php

review.reviewBody:
Everything about our dinner was excellent. The food was both interesting and delicious from
Start to finish. For example, the tomato salad had superior quality tomatoes with a tasty dressing followed by a scallop cake also accompanied by a delicious tarter sauce. And the portions were generous.

First time trying Kali Steak. We had a great meal. I booked for my daughter’s 25th birthday… just the two of us. We arrived a half hour early for an 8pm reservation… we were seated right away. It feels like a speakeasy… very dark and intimate… I liked the vibe. Service is casual put friendly and efficient. We shared a Caesar Salad and Shrimp Cocktail… both were outstanding. Then we shared a large porterhouse steak… perfectly cooked… great flavor. Creamed spinach was lovely. I will be back

Kali Steak is one of those places you could easily miss if you didn’t know what you were looking for—the exterior is pretty unassuming, but once you’re inside, it’s a completely different story. The space is beautiful, with warm lighting and thoughtful touches like individual table lamps that make the whole experience feel intimate and elevated. The valet tucked around the back was also a nice convenience.

Having just come off a flight, a double espresso was much needed to start the dinner, and it came hot and quickly with a cool spoonful of raw sugar. The espresso was fresh and delicious. The cocktail program stood out right away, especially their martini options. The level of customization and combinations made it feel more like an experience than just ordering a drink.

We started with the steak tartare, which was unlike any I’ve had before—in a good way. It leaned into Asian/Korean flavors, which gave it a unique twist that really worked. For the main, we shared one of the daily selection 24 oz steaks, and that was absolutely the right call for two people. Perfect portion, and cooked exactly how you’d want it.

On the side, the scalloped potatoes were a highlight—super soft, creamy, and honestly one of the best versions of that dish I’ve had. We finished with the signature Kali meringue gelato, which was definitely interesting, especially with the candied egg yolk on top. It’s a bit unconventional, but it works and makes for a memorable dessert.

Service was solid overall—attentive without being overbearing. All in all, Kali Steak delivers a really well-rounded experience with some unique touches that set it apart.
Excellent place to watch the Dodgers and have an outstanding burger and martini at the bar.
The food was amazing, service was top notch. Chef Meehan has an amazing restaurant.
Everything was absolutely perfect! From drinks to appetizers, steaks and desserts.
Excelente nos encantó mucho. Gracias por todo!!!!!!
Great place!   Food was amazing, service was outstanding and we even spent a little time talking with the owner.  Highly recommend the steak tartare - best ever.
Excellent, definitely worth the Michelin star! The staff is terrific and our waitress was awesome!

the steak was splendid. The only shortfall is limited of food and wine offerings. The appetizer selection is below par which makes this Michelin nominated restaurant a bit below par compares to other comparable.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Kali Steak is a strong choice for date night. The dining room is intimate and elegant (plush seating, booths, red-carpeted dining room) while the bar is lively if you prefer a more social vibe. Guests praise the carefully crafted cocktails, martinis, and attentive service, and many call it a special-occasion spot. Note: some guests report louder nights and occasional sports on a bar screen, so request the dining room or an early reservation for a quieter evening.

mainEntity.name: What are the portion sizes like at this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portions vary by dish: steaks are generously sized (menu lists 10–32 oz cuts including a 16 oz Ribeye and 32 oz porterhouse/ribeye), often suitable for sharing. Starters and sides are moderate, guests often recommend skipping the basic sides and ordering more distinctive or indulgent options. Several guests described portions as plentiful for multi-course tasting menus, while a few felt some sides were smaller than expected for the price.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant serve alcohol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Kali has a full bar, an extensive wine list and craft cocktails. Guests frequently praise the martinis and sommelier-driven wine suggestions; the wine menu includes high-end Champagne, Burgundy, and a broad selection by the bottle and glass. Expect classic steakhouse cocktails and knowledgeable wine service that many guests highlight as a strength.

mainEntity.name: What is this restaurant's stand-out or favorite dish?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Kali Meringue Gelato is one of the most frequently mentioned standouts, guests rave about it as a must-try dessert. Other crowd favorites include the beef tartare, shrimp cocktail, ribeye and porterhouse steaks, Parker House rolls, and seasonal small plates like scallop ceviche or mushroom risotto. Many guests highlight the desserts and the steak accompaniments as memorable.

mainEntity.name: What are this restaurant's opening hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kali Steak serves dinner on select nights: Wed–Sat from 6:00 pm to 9:30 pm, and Sunday from 6:00 pm to 9:00 pm. Because the restaurant focuses on evening service and occasionally runs special holiday or tasting events, it’s a good idea to check availability and book in advance.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have accessible or family-friendly seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Families and kids do dine at Kali, guests note the restaurant’s website and reviews call it kid-friendly and that groups often celebrate birthdays or bring teens. The restaurant accepts large parties and private bookings, so family celebrations are accommodated. Specific accessibility features (wheelchair access, ADA seating) aren’t listed in the provided information, so call ahead to confirm any mobility or special seating needs.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Kali Steak?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a quieter, more intimate experience, midweek nights (Wednesday–Thursday) or early dinner seatings are best. Weekends and nights with large parties or events can be lively and noisier, guests frequently note busy weekend energy, bar activity, and occasional loudly celebrating groups. If you want a calm meal, request the dining room and an early reservation.

mainEntity.name: What seating arrangements/rooms does this restaurant have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kali is arranged as a split space: a lively full bar area and an elegant dining room hidden behind a red curtain with plush seating and booths. The restaurant accepts private parties and can accommodate larger groups or banquets, and guests describe cozy booths and intimate table seating in the dining room.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kali blends old-school steakhouse charm with modern polish: expect dim, plush dining rooms, burgundy booths, jazz or curated playlists, and a lively bar. Many guests praise the classic-steakhouse vibe and elegant presentation, though some note the space can feel loud or busy on certain nights and that a bar screen/sports have appeared at times. Overall it’s a stylish, special-occasion atmosphere with two distinct moods (bar vs dining room).

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Kali Steak?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casual dress, the restaurant lists its dress code as casual, but many guests choose to dress up for the steakhouse’s intimate, special-occasion vibe. If you have a specific event or private party, you can check ahead for any additional expectations.

mainEntity.name: Can I make any special requests before I arrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Kali accommodates special requests and private events. Guests report the team (including the manager and sommelier) helping curate menus for birthdays and large groups, and the restaurant accepts private-party bookings. For dietary needs, seating preferences, cake or celebration arrangements, call the restaurant in advance so staff can prepare.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant kid-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, families do dine here and guests note Kali’s site says kids are welcome. While the menu focuses on steakhouse fare and refined small plates rather than a children’s menu, many families bring teens or celebrate birthdays here. For younger children, consider an early seating or booking a private room to ensure a comfortable experience.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Busiest: weekend nights and evenings with large parties or celebrations, guests frequently describe busy, loud weekends and energetic bar scenes. mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Heritage is a popular choice for date nights and special occasions. Guests frequently celebrate anniversaries and birthdays here, praising the tasting menu, attentive service, and thoughtful wine pairings. Expect an intimate, cozy setting in a converted craftsman house and a relaxed, unpretentious fine-dining vibe. Note: the room can get lively and sometimes loud when full, and the front/kitchen area can be smoky; consider asking for counter seating or an earlier reservation for a quieter, more romantic experience.

mainEntity.name: What are the portion sizes like at this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portions follow a multi-course tasting-menu format, small, carefully plated courses meant to be enjoyed as a progression rather than large single entrees. Guests note there are many courses (often a dozen) and some have felt satisfied while others said portions can feel light, especially if you’re very hungry. Wine pairing and pacing add to the fullness of the meal; if you prefer bigger plates, plan on a snack afterward or check current menu notes before you go.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have accessible or family-friendly seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Family-friendly: yes, families and guests sometimes celebrate birthdays and bring teens, many people use Heritage for special family occasions. Accessible seating: not clearly stated. The restaurant is a converted 1922 craftsman house with small dining rooms and a front entry; some guests mention stairs and a compact layout. If accessibility is important, call ahead so staff can confirm accommodations and seating options.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Heritage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Midweek or an earlier seating is often best for a quieter experience. Guests report that early week or earlier dinner seats (for example, an early Tuesday seating) tend to be calmer, while Friday–Saturday evenings fill up and can get lively and loud. If you want to watch the chefs, request bar/counter seating at the open kitchen; if you want a quieter table, ask for a room away from the kitchen when booking.

mainEntity.name: What seating arrangements/rooms does this restaurant have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Heritage features a small, lively indoor dining room in a converted craftsman house plus bar/chef’s counter seating overlooking an open kitchen and live-fire Santa Maria grill. Guests describe a front room near the kitchen (which can be smoky) and a secondary dining area; counter seats (3–4) offer the best view of kitchen action. Seating is intimate and compact, so if you prefer more space, ask about table location when you reserve.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Heritage feels cozy, warm, and unpretentious, a fine-dining tasting experience in a homey craftsman setting. Guests praise the inventive food, friendly service, and relaxed vibe (some even call it approachable Michelin dining). Expect lively energy: the room can become noisy when full, and guests note occasional smoke from the open kitchen and upbeat music (sometimes hip-hop). It’s intimate and celebratory, ideal for special nights with a casual-dress atmosphere.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Heritage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casual dress, the restaurant lists “Casual Dress” as the recommended attire. Guests often dress up for special occasions, but the overall atmosphere is relaxed rather than formal. That makes Heritage easy to visit for date nights and celebrations without needing black-tie attire.

mainEntity.name: Can I make any special requests before I arrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partially, Heritage asks guests to specify all dietary restrictions and allergies when booking and will make note of them, but the kitchen politely declines menu modifications and substitutions. If you have serious allergies, call ahead so staff can confirm whether they can safely accommodate you. For seating requests (quiet table or counter), mention those when you reserve, the team is helpful but space is limited.

mainEntity.name: Is this restaurant kid-friendly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Families do dine at Heritage, and guests often bring teens or celebrate birthdays with children. Because Heritage is a multi-course tasting-menu restaurant with small, tightly spaced tables and no kids’ menu, it’s best suited to older children who can sit through a longer tasting experience. If you’re visiting with younger kids, consider an early seating, the chef’s counter for a fun view, or call ahead to discuss suitability.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Busiest: Friday and Saturday evenings and any peak special-date evenings, guests frequently say the room fills up and gets lively (and louder). Quietest: early week nights and earlier dinner seatings (Tuesdays/early weekday evenings) tend to be calmer. If you want a quieter meal, book a midweek or early seating and request a table away from the kitchen when you reserve.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to Heritage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Midweek, Tuesday through Thursday, is often the best bet for a quieter, more relaxed experience. Many guests mention that early-midweek reservations feel calmer and let you better hear menu descriptions and enjoy the pacing, while Friday and Saturday evenings are more festive and louder if you prefer atmosphere over quiet.

mainEntity.name: Who owns Heritage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Heritage is family-owned and operated by Chef Philip Pretty and his sister, Lauren Pretty. The team emphasizes seasonal produce, sustainable sourcing, and a connected farm-to-table approach through their nearby Heritage Farm.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have private dining?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Heritage lists that it does not offer private-party spaces, though it does accept larger parties. The venue is small and intimate, with counter seating and two compact dining rooms rather than a separate private dining room. For special requests or group bookings, call the restaurant to discuss options and availability.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any special awards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Heritage has received Michelin recognition and sustainability honors. The restaurant lists a MICHELIN 1 Star (2023 and 2024) and MICHELIN Green 2024. Guests frequently reference its Michelin-starred status and praise the chef-driven, seasonal tasting menus and wine pairings.

content.body: Boia De is what you get when you combine the collective talents of two chefs trained in the kitchens of Scarpetta, Carbone, Animal, Son of a Gun, Eleven Madison Park, and The Nomad. Chefs Luciana Giangrandi and Alex Meyer have created a true delight, nestled in the middle of a shopping complex. Don't sleep on the incredible pastas.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Boia De is a funky, modern Italian restaurant situated in a shopping plaza in Little Haiti. Chef partners Luciana Giangrandi and Alex Meyer provide a warm welcome in a charming, eclectic and intimate space with a menu that encourages sharing. The term “locally-sourced” takes on new meaning at Boia De – with everything from freshly baked bread to custom plates acquired from nearby friends and colleagues.

need_to_know.body:
Reservations come available at noon each day for the dinner service 30 days in the future. 

We accommodate reservations with both our counter seating and tables.  While we do our best to accommodate, we cannot guarantee seating preferences. You can make a Counter/Table request in the notes of your reservation. 

We cannot guarantee our ability to modify the reservation from the way it was originally booked. For example, if you book two smaller tables in order to be a larger party, we cannot guarantee that you will be sat together.

We have a zero tolerance policy for reservations purchased through Appointment Trader. Any reservation that is found for sale will be cancelled in advance, and seating will not be guaranteed. 

As a courtesy to fellow diners we ask that: 
-Our furry friends be sat outside, or stay at home for dinner. We are an intimate space and want to ensure the comfort of ALL of our diners, including those with allergies. 
-Please let us know in advance if you will be bringing a service animal so we can do our best to accommodate your needs. 
-Please include children of all ages in your reservation request, and let us know in advance if you will be bringing a stroller. 

Cancellation policy- 
We ask our guests to cancel existing reservations 3 hours or more from the reservation time. Reservations that are cancelled within the 3 hour window, or not at all, are subject to a $20 per person charge. 

If you arrive with more guests than you booked for, we cannot guarantee accommodation. You will be charged a cancellation/no show fee if we are unable to seat you.

We accommodate walk-ins on a first come, first served basis but reservations are recommended.

Parking is free and plentiful.

about.body:
Papa Llama is a Michelin-starred Peruvian restaurant offering a modern and vibrant dining experience helmed by husband-and-wife team Kevin and Maria Ruiz, who draw inspiration from their Peruvian heritage and American upbringing to craft a "third culture" culinary journey. It is a kaleidoscopic tapestry of new peruvian cuisine, celebrating local and sustainably sourced ingredients.

Papa Llama also boasts an impressive natural wine program, featuring selections from organic and biodynamic vineyards tended by small, independent producers. The restaurant operates on a reservation-only basis for dinner service on select dates, ensuring a personalized and memorable dining experience.

2025 & 2024 MICHELIN Guide 1 Star
2022/ 2023 MICHELIN Guide Bib Gourmand Recipient. 
2022/ 2021 Orlando Sentinel Critic's Choice, Best Latin Restaurant.

ld_json.name: Camille
ld_json.description:
Camille offers an intimate dining experience with an 8-seat chef’s counter, four cozy booths, and an exclusive private dining room. The concept features a seasonal, multi-course menu that offers a contemporary twist on Vietnamese cuisine with French influences. Set in the picturesque Baldwin Park, the restaurant combines elegance with a unique culinary perspective.

"Camille takes the vibrant food culture of Vietnam and presents it in a more refined, progressive form. I want guests to leave feeling like they've experienced the historical culinary connection between French and Vietnamese cuisine." - Chef Tung Phan

ld_json.name: Koya
ld_json.description: Koya is an intimate 8 seat tasting menu only experience by Chefs Eric & Adriana Fralick. Our tasting menu is a focus on superior ingredients. In the Japanese culture, the peak season of a particular ingredient is called its shun (旬) and the shun of many ingredients are passionately anticipated each year. At Koya, you can expect to experience the concept of shun as our ever changing hyper seasonal and thematic menu will continue honoring tradition while showcasing new techniques. The tasting bar at Koya is like a stage, where every element of design is meant to highlight the theatre of the tasting experience.

ld_json.name: Kōsen
ld_json.description:
NOW SERVING OUR SPRING MENU. 

Kōsen, meaning “a ray of light," is rooted in the idea of clarity, precision, and quiet brilliance. This philosophy guides every element of the experience, from the composition of each course to the architecture of the space. Awarded a 1-MICHELIN Star for two consecutive years, Kōsen reflects the vision of Executive Chef Andrew Huang, whose approach balances tradition with innovation, delivering a refined Japanese concept to Tampa Heights.

Sustainability is not a feature, but a cornerstone of our restaurant ethos. Our kitchen operates with intention - through an evolving in-house fermentation program, close relationships with regenerative farmers, and a move away from single-use materials. What remains is a philosophy of care: for ingredients, for process, and for the world that sustains them.

For private party & event inquiries contact info@kosentampa.com

We do not accept cash.  A 20% service charge will be added to your final bill.

content.body: Michelin-starred in two cities — the Design District and original NYC outpost have many accolades between them — Cote marries the best of Korean barbecue with American steakhouse panache. That means steak tartare and caviar service, but also a “butcher’s feast,” which features four cuts of meat with an array of sides, and a 10-course steak omakase menu. It’s really a choose-your-own-adventure for carnivores.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: COTE, the Michelin-starred and James Beard Award-nominated KOREAN STEAKHOUSE™ and vision of proprietor Simon Kim, The restaurant emulates its flagship New York City-based locale synonymous with marrying the fun and fire of Korean barbecue with the hallmarks of a classic, regal American steakhouse. The result is a unique and convivial and interactive atmosphere, accompanied by the highest quality USDA Prime beef, an impeccable 1200+ label wine list, and a show-stopping beverage program.

need_to_know.body:
On Mother's Day, we are exclusively hosting a special Mother's Day Feast priced at $145 per person.

At COTE Miami, each experience is thoughtfully curated. Our grill-top dining tables are designed for parties of four or more, creating the perfect setting for shared indulgence and elevated connection. 

Our tables tend to book quickly far in advance, so walk-ins are contingent upon cancellations & no shows. Smaller party reservations are welcomed within our first and last seating of the evening. 

We kindly ask that all guests arrive promptly. A 15-minute grace period is extended; however, we ask that everyone in the party arrives before seating so the entire party can enjoy the experience together.

Planning a party of 7 or more? Head over to the link on the right under “Other Ways to Support Cote Miami,” and our events team will reach back out shortly.

Planning what to wear to COTE?  While swimwear and cover-ups aren’t permitted, we invite you to embrace a polished, casual chic aesthetic for your visit.

To preserve the integrity of the COTE experience, we strictly prohibit unauthorized reservation transfers, bot-assisted bookings, and third-party reservation sales. Any such reservations will be canceled and reported directly to Resy. Third-party bookings will not be honored.

ld_json.name: Ariete
ld_json.description: Ours is a story only Miami can tell. It’s about lands far away but not forgotten, a culture we’re building as we put down roots, and the heights we can reach. Executive Chef and Owner Michael Beltran’s vision — shaped by passion for his Cuban heritage, devotion to championing Miami ingredients and tradition, and commitment to classic French technique — guides one of the city’s most talented restaurant teams in every dish, every drink, every moment at Ariete.Most important, though, is that you experience delicious food. That you escape. That you feel welcome in our home. Take a ride through a tasting menu or experience our canard à la presse in our dining room. Join us at the bar for our Florida Orange and a cocktail.From our corner of Coconut Grove, we’ve sent a message: Miami has a place at the global culinary table. In 2022, we put a Michelin Star on the wall. The world is listening.This is Miami’s food story. We invite you to join us in writing the next chapter.

review.reviewBody: My reservation at Ariete exceeded my expectations. The staff was incredibly hospitable and ensured a special experience. The food was memorable in the best way possible, and their Michelin Star is well deserved. I hope to come back whenever I return to the area. Shout out to Cameron for going above and beyond to contribute to such a special experience.
Excellent!!! We did the tasting menu-everything was properly prtioned and delicious.  Highly recommend.
Very nice night. Flan is quite special, with very unique flavors
I absolutely loved this place, my boyfriend is a foodie so decided to take him here as a Christmas present. The food was excellent, the service was exceptional.

Very cool place , food excellent , service excellent and great warm vibe
Also Coconut grove area very charming

Me experience was wonderful. And the food was espectacular. I ordered oysters and venison the preparation was perfect and the taste incredible.
The service was perfect they explained each dish.
The dessert was flan and was divine food fit for the gods.

Relaxed neighborhood feel, but food and service that warrant its star.  The wine director took my mumbled comments about limestone and structure and set me on a fantastic white Burgandy.  The oyster dish was excellent.  My wife ordered a vegetable crudite (I was worried about this decision!) and it was excellent, with a variety of tastes and textures.  We wound up with something like four apps and two entrees and enjoyed a cross section of the menu.  It was really a lot of fun.

If I can offer any constructive feedback it’s that the place is really quite small.  It doesn’t feel like an event and you may sit close to a door or some other feature you’d rather be away from.  It’s also really casual.  Part of that is Miami.  But it’s something to be aware of.
Delicious and unique menu; great staff and customer service
Normally this restaurant could be quiet but the karaoke bar next door hijacked the out door dining.

Overall experience was good. They must have been working on some bathroom pipes because it stunk sitting indoors which they apologized for. They did serve my wife a plate with something she was allergic to and the manager literally ran over and snatched the plate as she was cutting into it.

ld_json.description: Soseki is a Michelin-starred modern omakase experience that blends time-honored Japanese tradition with the vibrant seasonality of Central Florida. With just 10 seats, the intimate dining room allows chefs to present a thoughtfully curated multi-course tasting menu that evolves with the region’s growing cycles. The experience celebrates local farms and purveyors while honoring the simplicity and precision of piece-by-piece nigiri. Recognized with one Michelin Star, Soseki continues to push the boundaries of what omakase can be in Florida.

review.reviewBody: The chefs menu provided a delightful variety of of small bites and shareable plates.it was all absolutely delicious but my favorite bites were the Fontina French Toast and the Mushroom Ravioli. The meal was topped off by a very tasty Chocolate Mousse with custard and torched marshmallow. I thoroughly enjoyed sitting at the window to people watch as the evening unfolded
Fantastic small plates/tapas style menu. Great service, great atmosphere.  We went for the set menu. Great value at €55 per head. Highly recommended

I am so happy I did the chef’s menu with the wine pairing. Not a single dish I didn’t like. I think this was a very well-thought-out menu; every dish outdoes the previous one, and the portions are just right. The mushroom ravioli and pork cheek dish were my favourites. I have to say that I had the most perfectly cooked steak here, and I’ve been to 3 other highly regarded steakhouses in Dublin—it melts in your mouth. I really enjoyed this experience and would recommend it to anyone who wants a special food-and-wine experience in the city!

We enjoyed the chefs menu and had a fantastic meal. Service and atmosphere were all faultless and the food was excellent with such a variety of interesting flavours. Definitely will be recommending to friends visiting Dublin.

Hands-down the best meal I've had in Ireland. I looked this place up beforehand, and it completely exceeded my expectations.
The dishes were incredibly innovative — unique flavor pairings, contrasting textures, creative styles, and impressive techniques that showed real depth and skill. Nothing felt unapproachable or overly fussy, yet every bite highlighted the chefs' expertise. This is one of those rare experiences I know will stand the test of time as one of my all-time favorites.
The cool, trendy location is perfect for people-watching, and it was a treat to see the chefs in action right in front of you. Service was spot-on: warm, friendly, and perfectly balanced — professional yet playful and fun. The stylish decor, outstanding food, and great music came together to create the ideal atmosphere for great conversation and a genuinely memorable night out.
Highly recommend!
The food was outstanding, visually and taste wise. The service personnel was very attentive and nice. We will definitely go back.

Great food , service and vibe. The only complaint is the seating . The fixed seats are too close to the bar  - adequate but a tad uncomfortable. Apart from that the excellent food and service more than made up for it .
The restaurant deserves a bigger space ✌️
Excellent experience! Creative dishes, and cocktails. Fun location, friendly Staff. Treat yourself!

I ate here with a friend in April 2026.  Overall a bit disappointing, we expected better based on reviews and  because it has a bib gourmand.  None of our dishes were particularly memorable, they just weren't particularly tasty, and they needed to be served warmer.  The vibe and service were good however, and price wise its reasonable.  But overall neither of us are in a rush to go back, which is a pity, maybe they just had a off night.
Fabulous venue, delish food, fantastic service. Really relaxed and vibey atmosphere. Would highly recommend a visit.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amy Austin has a lively, buzzy and intimate atmosphere, energetic rather than formal. Guests frequently describe it as cosy, stylish and fun, with a busy open kitchen and upbeat music. It can be loud at peak times because the room is small and close-packed, which adds to the buzz but may not suit those seeking a quiet dinner. Overall the vibe is informal, convivial and chef-driven.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any special awards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Amy Austin was awarded the MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2024. Guests and guides have noted the restaurant’s inventive, high-quality small plates and wine focus, which aligns with the Bib Gourmand recognition for good value and quality.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Amy Austin?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casual dress is the norm. Guests tend to dress smart-casual for the intimate, buzzy setting, you don’t need formal wear but many people opt for neat outfits for an evening out. The restaurant listing specifies a casual dress code.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Amy Austin?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a slightly quieter experience, aim for a weekday (Mon–Thu) early evening or Friday lunchtime; evenings on Fri and Sat are the busiest and buzziest. Many guests praise the atmosphere at the counter but note peak nights are loud and packed. If you prefer watching the kitchen without the full crowd, request bar seating and book in advance; midweek bookings usually feel more relaxed.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Amy Austin is a popular choice for a lively, intimate date night. The venue is small and stylish with a chefs’ counter and window seats that are great for people-watching. Expect sharing small plates, creative flavours, good wines (including wine on tap) and a buzzy atmosphere that many guests describe as fun and memorable. Book in advance and ask for a window or counter seat if you want a more theatrical experience; be aware it can get loud at peak times.

mainEntity.name: What are the portion sizes like at this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portions are small, tapas-style plates meant for sharing. Guests consistently mention ordering multiple plates (recommendation: 2–3 plates per person) to make a full meal. Some guests loved the flavour but said some dishes felt pricey for their size, while others found five dishes between two people fine when budgeting accordingly. If you’re hungry, plan to order several small plates or add extras.

mainEntity.name: What seating arrangements/rooms does this restaurant have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amy Austin is a compact, counter-forward space with a chefs’ counter, window seating and a few high tables. Seating is primarily high stools and counter spots that let you watch the kitchen in action, guests love the front-row experience. There aren’t private dining rooms; the layout is intimate and tightly arranged, so larger groups may be split across tables. Book ahead and request preferred seating when you reserve.

mainEntity.name: Can I make any special requests before I arrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can and should call ahead for special requests. Guests report staff are attentive with dietary needs and celebrations (some guests received birthday extras and staff helped with allergies), so the team will usually accommodate allergies, dietary requirements and celebration requests where possible. Because seating is tight, note any accessibility or seating preferences when booking so they can advise you.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Busiest: Friday and Saturday evenings (popular, loud, often fully booked). Quietest: weekday evenings (Mon–Thu) and Friday lunchtime when available. Guests frequently note high demand on weekend nights and recommend midweek bookings for a more relaxed pace. If you prefer a calmer meal, choose a weekday or an earlier seating.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have private dining?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not as a private room, Amy Austin does not offer private dining spaces, and the restaurant describes itself as a small wine bar. It does, however, accept larger parties where space allows, though the compact layout can mean groups are split across seating. Contact the team before booking larger groups to confirm availability and seating arrangements.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to Amy Austin?

acceptedAnswer.text: Aim for a weekday evening (Tuesday–Thursday) for the best balance of atmosphere and a slightly calmer service. Many guests praise midweek visits as more relaxed, while Friday and Saturday nights are lively but much busier, great if you want a vibrant scene but expect noise and fuller seating. If you want less crowd and more time, choose midweek.

mainEntity.name: How is Amy Austin restaurant rated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amy Austin is rated 4.6 stars by 613 OpenTable diners.

mainEntity.name: Does Amy Austin offer gift cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amy Austin does offer gift cards which you can purchase here.

mainEntity.name: Is Amy Austin currently accepting bookings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can generally book this restaurant by choosing the date, time and party size on OpenTable.

item.name: Turas Fíona: Wines of Central Europe
item.description:
As part of Blas na Bealtaine, A Taste of Galway, join us at Daróg Wine Bar for Turas Fíona, a wine journey through Central Europe with Zsolt Lukács, Michelin Sommelier of the Year 2025, and food and wine writer Cathal McBride.

Central Europe holds a special place in Zsolt’s story and continues to shape the wine philosophy at Daróg. This relaxed and informative tasting explores a region known for its diversity, indigenous grape varieties and strong sense of place. Throughout the evening, Zsolt and Cathal will guide guests through a curated wine flight of five wines, paired with a cheese board, while exploring the relationship between wine and food, and sharing insights into the regions, traditions and producers behind each glass.

Please note the kitchen will be closed for the evening and the regular menu will not be available.

organizer.name: Daróg Wine Bar
organizer.description: Daróg Wine Bar (Irish: small oak tree) opened its doors in July 2023 in the heart of Galway city. Daróg is a place built around sharing good wine, food, and conversation. Brought to life by husband-and-wife team Zsolt and Edel Lukács, it’s a space shaped by shared passions — for wine, food, and art. In 2025, Daróg received a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, while Zsolt was named MICHELIN Sommelier of the Year for Great Britain & Ireland. The bar was also recognised by Wine Spectator with an Award of Excellence, and named Wine Experience of the Year by Georgina Campbell.

item.name: Le Chéile with Siobhán Moore
item.description:
As part of her Exhibition, join Siobhan Moore and Edel Lukács for Le Chéile: An Evening of Creative Conversation. 

“Le Chéile” means “together” in Irish—and that’s exactly what these evenings at Daróg are about. A space to slow down, connect, and share stories through wine and art.

Artist Talk
On the night, Siobhán will join Edel in conversation. This guided discussion explores the artist's practices, materials and connection to landscape.

Wine Tasting
To accompany the evening, one of our sommeliers will guide you through a tasting of two glasses of wine selected to complement the evening. There’ll be time to chat, ask questions, and view (or purchase) the work in a relaxed and intimate setting.

Pop-Up Art Shop
A selection of original works & prints, will also be available to purchase on the night — a chance to pick up something special.

✨ Guests will receive 10% off all artwork purchases made on the night. ✨

Tickets: €20 per person
Booking essential

mainEntity.name: What is this restaurant's stand-out or favorite dish?

acceptedAnswer.text: There isn’t a single dish mentioned consistently by guests, instead, visitors praise the overall food and the expertly paired wines. The menu features standout small plates like wild Irish venison loin, scallop with yuzu miso, Dexter beef tartare and Ibérico de Bellota, so ask staff for the evening’s favourite plates and recommended wine pairings.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant serve alcohol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Daróg is a dedicated wine bar with a highly regarded, curated wine list. Guests repeatedly praise the wine selection and the staff’s wine advice; the owner/sommelier has been recognised (MICHELIN Sommelier of the Year) and the bar has received Wine Spectator recognition.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to go to Daróg Wine Bar?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a quieter experience aim for Tuesday–Thursday evenings when the bar opens at 17:00. If you want a livelier atmosphere and a longer menu window, visit Friday–Sunday (opens from 15:00). Guests often highlight personalised service and a relaxed, intimate vibe, arriving earlier on weekend days can also help if you prefer a less busy table.

mainEntity.name: What are the portion sizes like at this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portions are small-plate style and geared toward sharing or ordering several dishes per person. The menu is organised under “Small Plates” and “Snacks, ” and guests describe the offerings as “great small bites, ” so plan to order a few plates to make a full meal or enjoy a tasting-style evening paired with wine.

mainEntity.name: What are this restaurant's opening hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: Daróg is open evenings: Tuesday–Thursday 17:00–23:00, Friday–Sunday 15:00–23:00. Those hours make it a great spot for early evening drinks or a later dinner on weekends.

mainEntity.name: Is this a good pick for date night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Daróg is a popular, intimate wine bar that’s well suited to date night. Guests consistently praise the food, personalised service and an outstanding wine list, and the space is described as casual-elegant and built around sharing wine, food and conversation. It also holds a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand and awards for its wine program, which makes it a great choice if you want a memorable evening of small plates and expertly chosen wines.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have vegan/vegetarian, gluten-free or other dietary options?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, there are clearly labelled vegetarian options on the menu (several items marked “(v)” such as Roast potatoes with rosemary, St. Tola goat’s curd and Crispy polenta with black truffle). Vegan and gluten-free options aren’t explicitly listed, so if you have strict dietary needs call ahead, the team can advise on ingredient substitutions or suitable plates.

mainEntity.name: What seating arrangements/rooms does this restaurant have?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are no private dining rooms, but Daróg accepts larger groups and is set up for shared dining around small plates and wine. The space is described as casual-elegant and designed for conversation and tasting rather than formal private events, if you need a specific layout for a group, it’s best to contact the team directly.

mainEntity.name: What is the best day to go to Daróg Wine Bar?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you want a quieter, intimate evening, choose a Tuesday–Thursday night. For a livelier late-afternoon or weekend experience, visit Friday–Sunday when the bar opens from 15:00. Both options highlight great food and an outstanding wine list, so pick based on whether you prefer calm or buzz.

mainEntity.name: What is the dress code for Daróg Wine Bar?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dress code is casual dress. Guests typically wear smart-casual attire appropriate for a relaxed, elegant wine bar.

mainEntity.name: What's the ambience/atmosphere like in this restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Daróg offers an intimate, casual-elegant atmosphere focused on conversation, wine and small plates. Guests describe attentive, personal service and an enthusiastic owner who curates the wine list, overall it’s warm, relaxed and ideal for food-and-wine-focused evenings.

mainEntity.name: When is this restaurant busiest and quietest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Daróg is likely busiest on weekend afternoons and evenings (Friday–Sunday, when it opens earlier), and quieter during weekday evenings (Tuesday–Thursday). Guests praise a memorable, attentive experience, so if you prefer a calmer visit choose a midweek booking or an earlier weekend seating.

mainEntity.name: Does this restaurant have any specials deals or experiences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Daróg is best known for its curated wine programme and small-plate dining experience rather than fixed discount deals. The bar has received awards (MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, Wine Spectator Award of Excellence, Wine Experience of the Year), and guests highlight excellent wine pairings, contact the team or check their website for any tasting events or seasonal experiences.

content.body: The restaurant that introduced D.C. to ramen almost 14 years ago is still as essential as ever. Critically-acclaimed mainstay Toki Underground continues to draw inspiration from the noodle soups of Japan, doling out flavorful broths that’ll have you slurping to your heart’s content. Must-orders include the fried chicken steamed buns, chicken curry ramen, and the garlic mala tonkotsu, but don’t skip any of the other small izakaya-inspired plates (gluten-free and vegan options included), alongside a solid list of cocktails and sake.
content.name: why_we_like_it

Dining here means fresh-baked breads, pastries and a vegetable-centric menu featuring house-fermented ingredients. The beverage program highlights coffee from small-batch roasters, craft cocktails, and artisanal & biodynamic wines.

content.body: At Maketto, Erik Bruner-Yang puts his stamp on Cambodian and Taiwanese eats, spinning dim sum, noodles, and fried chicken like no other. Gather a crew, and eat your way through the menu; there isn’t a single dish we wouldn’t recommend.
content.name: why_we_like_it

about.body: Tom Sietsema says, "The dude who makes arguably the best ramen in town, at Toki Underground, turns out to be pretty deft with Taiwanese and Cambodian dishes, too. Erik Bruner-Yang took seemingly forever to open his second restaurant on H Street NE, but our patience paid off. When Maketto began serving steamed buns with shredded pork and Khmer-style meat dip with crudite in April, the launch also unveiled...pedigreed pastries (Frenchie’s) and coffee (Vigilante) — lots to like under one cool roof. I’m usually here for dinner on the ground floor, somewhere in a dining room that starts with a bar and spills onto a patio followed by an open kitchen with slender counters. And if my job didn’t require me to eat the full menu, I could happily stick to just the fried, five-spice chicken, that warm dip enriched with coconut milk and curry, and a Wagyu bao platter that goes down like Asian roast beef sandwiches. Come with an open mind. Ground duck hearts, brined in nuoc cham and smoky from the grill, could become your new best friend."

tagline.body: One of the biggest openings of the year." –Washingtonian Magazine

ld_json.name: L'Ardente
ld_json.description:
A timeless Italian culinary experience for this moment.

Glittering chandeliers float below wooden farm beams. Wisps of fragrant smoke linger inside a gold-plated pizza oven. Sumptuous fabrics meet impeccable ingredients.

This is L’Ardente, the latest hospitality venture from the award-winning team behind Unconventional Diner. The restaurant reflects the glorious contrasts of Italy itself: haute yet simple; glam yet rustic; indulgent yet restrained. Above all, it’s a destination DC deserves right now, a Mediterranean balm in the heart of the capital.

Residents is a multi-sensory experience that involves all five senses: vision, touch, sound, smell, and taste. To include curated house playlists throughout the day and into the night. We use greenery to create a stunning and perfect ambiance with a beautiful array of plants. We are excited to host you!

need_to_know.body:
Thank you for considering a reservation at Residents Cafe & Bar. Please take a moment to review the following information before making your reservation:

Residents Cafe & Bar is a high-energy dining and cocktail experience. The ambiance and music are an integral part of the concept, and the music level may be slightly higher than in a traditional restaurant.

20% service charge is included on every tab. 18% is distributed directly to service workers on top of their base wages, and the remaining 2% is used to help pay for our staff costs, such as base wages, health insurance, etc. You may choose to leave an additional tip! 

For drinks only, we do offer bar-seating and tables for walk-ins.

While we do our best to honor reservations at the requested time, there may be a minimal wait with a reservation.

A credit card is required to secure a reservation. If you need to cancel your reservation, please do so at least 3 hours in advance to avoid a $25 per person cancellation fee.

We ask that parties arrive on time to fully experience Residents. We have a 15-minute grace period for reservations before releasing the table to our waitlist. Please arrive promptly to secure your reservation.

All brunch reservations reserve their table for 90 minutes.
All dinner reservations reserve their table for 2 hours.

why_we_like_it.body: The name here was inspired by the owners, all immigrants who settled in Washington. Come for the show-stopping cocktails, especially the espresso martini. There’s also a raft of bottled and seasonal cocktails and, if you’re so inclined, non-alcoholic versions of the espresso martini and ginger cocktails, too.

ld_json.description:
Looking for Thanksgiving Feasts? Please use DoorDash or Uber Eats to order from a limited quantity of  available packages! 

Located at 1207 9th St. NW on the ground floor of the Walter E. Washington Convention Center in D.C.’s Shaw neighborhood, the diner has been serving globally inspired comfort foods dreamed up by James Beard-nominated Chef David Deshaies and his team since 2017.

The extensive selection of diner favorites with modern twists has earned the restaurant a coveted spot on Michelin Guide’s Bib Gourmand list since 2018 and four RAMMY awards. The diner is open daily, serving popular brunch plates like chicken and waffles, blueberry-lavender buttermilk pancakes and corned-beef hash every day from 9 a.m.–3:45 p.m. Dinner runs from 4–10 p.m., offering such dishes as chicken parm “florentine,” meatloaf, fried chicken and Peking duck confit.

Find Unconventional Diner online at www.unconventionaldiner.com; on Instagram at @unconventionaldiner; on Twitter/X at @uncondiner; and on Facebook.
